bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 起強圉大淵獻，盡上章困敦，凡十四年。

translations.literal: From Qianggu Dayuanxian through Shangzhang Kundun; fourteen years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Qianggu Dayuanxian through Shangzhang Kundun—fourteen years in all.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，梁王來朝。

translations.literal: 1. In winter, the tenth month, the King of Liang came to court.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In winter, the tenth month, the King of Liang came to court.

sentences.zh: 時上未置太子，與梁王宴飲，從容言曰：「千秋萬歲後傳於王。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor had not yet installed a crown prince; feasting with the King of Liang, he spoke at ease, saying: "After a thousand autumns and ten thousand years I shall pass it to you, King.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had not yet named a crown prince. Over wine with the King of Liang he said lightly, "When a thousand autumns and ten thousand years have passed, I shall pass the throne to you, my king.

sentences.zh: 」王辭謝，雖知非至言，然心內喜，太后亦然。

translations.literal: " The king declined with thanks; though he knew these were not words meant in earnest, inwardly he was pleased, and the empress dowager likewise.
translations.idiomatic: " The king declined with thanks. Though he knew these were not words meant in earnest, inwardly he rejoiced—and so did the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 詹事竇嬰引卮酒進上曰：「天下者，高祖之天下，父子相傳，漢之約也，上何以得傳梁王！

translations.literal: Household intendant Dou Ying raised his cup of wine and advanced to the emperor, saying: "All under Heaven is Gaozu's all under Heaven; father passes to son—this is Han's covenant. How could Your Majesty pass it to the King of Liang!
translations.idiomatic: Household intendant Dou Ying raised his cup and stepped forward. "All under Heaven belongs to Gaozu," he said. "Father passes the realm to son—that is Han's covenant. How could Your Majesty pass it to the King of Liang!

sentences.zh: 」太后由此憎嬰。

translations.literal: " From this the empress dowager came to hate Dou Ying.
translations.idiomatic: " From that moment the empress dowager hated Dou Ying.

sentences.zh: 嬰因病免；

translations.literal: Dou Ying was dismissed on account of illness;
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying was dismissed, pleading illness;

sentences.zh: 太后除嬰門籍，不得朝請。

translations.literal: the empress dowager removed Dou Ying from the court registry and he could not attend audiences.
translations.idiomatic: and the empress dowager struck his name from the court registry so he could no longer attend audiences.

sentences.zh: 梁王以此益驕。

translations.literal: The King of Liang for this reason grew still more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Liang grew still more arrogant because of it.

sentences.zh: ----2春，正月，乙巳，赦。

translations.literal: ----2 In spring, the first month, on yisi, a pardon.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In spring, the first month, on the day yisi, a general pardon was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: ----3長星出西方。

translations.literal: ----3 A long comet appeared in the west.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 A long-tailed comet appeared in the west.

sentences.zh: ----4洛陽東宮災。

translations.literal: ----4 The Eastern Palace at Luoyang caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 Fire destroyed the Eastern Palace at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: ----5初，孝文時，吳太子入見，得侍皇太子飲、博。

translations.literal: ----5 At the outset, in Emperor Wen's time, the heir of Wu came in audience and was permitted to attend the crown prince in drinking and gaming.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 Earlier, in Emperor Wen's reign, the heir of Wu came to court and was allowed to drink and play board games with the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 吳太子博爭道，不恭；

translations.literal: The heir of Wu disputed the board in gaming and was disrespectful;
translations.idiomatic: During a game the heir of Wu disputed a move and behaved disrespectfully;

sentences.zh: 皇太子引博局提吳太子，殺之。

translations.literal: the crown prince seized the gaming board and struck the heir of Wu, killing him.
translations.idiomatic: the crown prince seized the board and struck the heir of Wu, killing him.

sentences.zh: 遣其喪歸葬，至吳，吳王慍曰：「天下同宗，死長安即葬長安，何必來葬為！

translations.literal: They sent the coffin back for burial; when it reached Wu, the King of Wu said angrily: "All under Heaven share one ancestry—if he died in Chang'an, bury him in Chang'an; why must you come here to bury!
translations.idiomatic: They sent the body home for burial. When the coffin reached Wu, the King of Wu said in anger, "We share one ancestry under Heaven. If he died in Chang'an, bury him in Chang'an—why drag him here to bury!

sentences.zh: 」復遣喪之長安葬。

translations.literal: " They again sent the coffin to Chang'an for burial.
translations.idiomatic: " They sent the coffin back to Chang'an for burial.

sentences.zh: 吳王由此稍失籓臣之禮，稱疾不朝。

translations.literal: The King of Wu for this reason gradually lapsed from a feudal subject's rites and claimed illness and did not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: From this the King of Wu gradually abandoned a vassal's courtesies, claiming illness and refusing to attend court.

sentences.zh: 京師知其以子故，系治、驗問吳使者；

translations.literal: The capital knew this was on account of his son and detained and interrogated Wu's envoys;
translations.idiomatic: The capital knew the cause was his son and detained and interrogated Wu's envoys;

sentences.zh: 吳王恐，始有反謀。

translations.literal: the King of Wu grew afraid and first formed plans of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: and the King of Wu, growing afraid, first conceived plans of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 後使人為秋請，文帝復問之，使者對曰：「王實不病；

translations.literal: Later someone was sent on autumn petition; Emperor Wen again questioned him, and the envoy replied: "The king is in fact not ill;
translations.idiomatic: Later an envoy came with the autumn petition. Emperor Wen questioned him again, and the envoy answered, "The king is not ill at all;

sentences.zh: 漢系治使者數輩，吳王恐，以故遂稱病。

translations.literal: Han has detained several envoys; the King of Wu was afraid and for that reason then claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: Han has detained several of our envoys. The King of Wu was afraid, and for that reason he claimed illness.

sentences.zh: 夫察見淵中魚不祥，唯上棄前過，與之更始。

translations.literal: To scrutinize so closely as to see fish in the depths is inauspicious; I pray Your Majesty discard former faults and grant him a fresh start.
translations.idiomatic: To see fish in a deep pool is inauspicious—too close a scrutiny. I pray Your Majesty discard former faults and grant him a fresh start.

sentences.zh: 」於是文帝乃赦吳使者，歸之，而賜吳王幾杖，老，不朝。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Emperor Wen pardoned Wu's envoys and sent them back, and bestowed on the King of Wu a staff of rest for old age, exempt from court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Emperor Wen pardoned Wu's envoys and sent them home, and bestowed on the King of Wu a cane of ease in old age, exempting him from court attendance.

sentences.zh: 吳得釋其罪，謀亦益解。

translations.literal: Wu was released from his guilt and the plot also gradually dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was released from blame, and the plot gradually dissolved as well.

sentences.zh: 然其居國，以銅、鹽故，百姓無賦；

translations.literal: Yet in his realm, on account of copper and salt, the common people paid no taxes;
translations.idiomatic: Yet within his realm, because of copper and salt, the common people paid no taxes;

sentences.zh: 卒踐更，輒予平賈；

translations.literal: when soldiers performed rotation duty, he at once paid fair market price;
translations.idiomatic: when soldiers performed corvée rotation, he paid them fair market wages;

sentences.zh: 歲時存問茂材，賞賜閭里；

translations.literal: at year's seasons he inquired after outstanding talent and rewarded village neighborhoods;
translations.idiomatic: at each season he inquired after outstanding men and rewarded the villages;

sentences.zh: 他郡國吏欲來捕亡人者，公共禁弗予。

translations.literal: when officials of other commanderies and states wished to come capture fugitives, he publicly forbade and would not yield them.
translations.idiomatic: when officials from other commanderies and kingdoms came to seize fugitives, he publicly forbade it and would not hand them over.

sentences.zh: 如此者四十餘年。

translations.literal: Thus for more than forty years.
translations.idiomatic: This went on for more than forty years.

sentences.zh: 晁錯數上書言吳過，可削；

translations.literal: Chao Cuo repeatedly submitted memorials saying Wu's faults could be cut away;
translations.idiomatic: Chao Cuo repeatedly memorialized that Wu's offenses warranted reduction;

sentences.zh: 文帝寬，不忍罰，以此吳日益橫。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was lenient and could not bear to punish; for this Wu daily grew more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was lenient and could not bear to punish him, and for this Wu grew daily more overbearing.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，錯說上曰：「昔高帝初定天下，昆弟少，諸子弱，大封同姓，齊七十餘城，楚四十餘城，吳五十餘城；

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Chao Cuo persuaded him, saying: "Of old when Gaodi first settled all under Heaven, brothers were few and sons weak; he greatly enfeoffed those of the same surname—Qi had more than seventy cities, Chu more than forty, Wu more than fifty;
translations.idiomatic: When the new emperor took the throne, Chao Cuo urged him: "When Gaodi first settled the realm, his brothers were few and his sons young. He enfeoffed kinsmen on a vast scale—Qi held more than seventy cities, Chu more than forty, Wu more than fifty;

sentences.zh: 封三庶孽，分天下半。

translations.literal: he enfeoffed three collateral lines and divided half all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: he enfeoffed three collateral lines and gave them half the realm.

sentences.zh: 今吳王前有太子之郤，詐稱病不朝，於古法當誅。

translations.literal: Now the King of Wu earlier had the matter of the crown prince's grudge, feigned illness and did not attend court—by ancient law he should be executed.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu already bears a grudge over the crown prince's killing of his heir, and he feigned illness to avoid court—by ancient law he should be executed.

sentences.zh: 文帝弗忍，因賜幾杖，德至厚，當改過自新，反益驕溢，即山鑄錢，煮海水為鹽，誘天下亡人謀作亂。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen could not bear it and therefore bestowed the rest-staff—grace reaching utmost depth; he should have changed his faults and renewed himself, but instead grew still more arrogant and excessive, minting coin by the mountains and boiling sea water for salt, luring all under Heaven's fugitives and plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen could not bear to punish him and instead bestowed a cane of ease—grace of the deepest kind. He should have mended his ways, but grew only more arrogant: minting coin in the hills, boiling seawater for salt, luring fugitives from across the realm, and plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 今削之亦反，不削亦反。

translations.literal: Now if you cut him he will rebel; if you do not cut him he will also rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Cut his territory and he will rebel; leave it uncut and he will rebel anyway.

sentences.zh: 削之，其反亟，禍小；

translations.literal: If you cut, his rebellion will be urgent but the calamity small;
translations.idiomatic: If you cut now, his rebellion will come soon but the calamity will be small;

sentences.zh: 不削，反遲，禍大。

translations.literal: if you do not cut, rebellion will be delayed but the calamity great.
translations.idiomatic: if you do not cut, rebellion will come late but the calamity will be great.

sentences.zh: 」上令公卿、列侯、宗室雜議，莫敢難；

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered the high ministers, ranked marquises, and imperial clan to debate together; none dared object;
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered the high ministers, ranked marquises, and imperial clan to debate the matter together. None dared object;

sentences.zh: 獨竇嬰爭之，由此與錯有郤。

translations.literal: only Dou Ying contested it, and from this he had a grudge with Chao Cuo.
translations.idiomatic: only Dou Ying argued against it, and from this he and Chao Cuo bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及楚王戊來朝，錯因言：「戊往年為薄太后服，私奸服舍，請誅之。

translations.literal: When King Wu of Chu came to court, Chao Cuo took occasion to say: "Wu in a past year for Empress Dowager Bo's mourning privately committed impropriety in the mourning lodge; I request he be executed.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu of Chu came to court, Chao Cuo seized the occasion to say, "In a past year Wu, while mourning Empress Dowager Bo, committed impropriety in the mourning lodge. I ask that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 」詔赦，削東海郡。

translations.literal: " An edict pardoned him and cut away Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict pardoned him but stripped away Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 及前年，趙王有罪，削其常山郡；

translations.literal: And in the year before last, the King of Zhao had guilt and Changshan commandery was cut away;
translations.idiomatic: The year before last the King of Zhao was found guilty and Changshan commandery was cut away;

sentences.zh: 膠西王卬以賣爵事有奸，削其六縣。

translations.literal: King Ying of Jiaoxi on account of selling ranks had impropriety and six counties were cut from him.
translations.idiomatic: King Ying of Jiaoxi was implicated in selling ranks and lost six counties.

sentences.zh: 廷臣方議削吳。

translations.literal: Court ministers were then debating cutting Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers were then debating how to reduce Wu.

sentences.zh: 吳王恐削地無已，因發謀舉事。

translations.literal: The King of Wu, fearing the cutting of territory would never end, thereupon launched his plot and raised the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu, fearing his lands would be cut without end, thereupon set his plot in motion.

sentences.zh: 念諸侯無足與計者，聞膠西王勇，好兵，諸侯皆畏憚之，於是使中大夫應高口說膠西王曰：「今者主上任用邪臣，聽信讒賊，侵削諸侯，誅罰良重，日以益甚。

translations.literal: Thinking no feudal lord was fit to plan with, he heard King Ying of Jiaoxi was brave and loved troops and that all feudal lords feared him; he therefore sent Central Grandee Ying Gao to speak and persuade King Ying of Jiaoxi, saying: "Now the ruler employs wicked ministers, listens to slanderers, invades and cuts feudal lords, punishments and executions very heavy, daily growing worse.
translations.idiomatic: He judged no other feudal lord fit to plot with, but heard that King Ying of Jiaoxi was brave, loved arms, and was feared by all the princes. He therefore sent Central Grandee Ying Gao to persuade him in person: "The Son of Heaven now employs wicked ministers, heeds slanderers, strips the feudal lords, and metes out ever heavier punishments day by day.

sentences.zh: 語有之曰：『狧糠及米。

translations.literal: There is a saying: 'When the thorny brush is scraped to the chaff, it reaches the grain.
translations.idiomatic: There is a saying: 'Scrape the chaff and you reach the grain.

sentences.zh: 』吳與膠西，知名諸侯也，一時見察，不得安肆矣。

translations.literal: ' Wu and Jiaoxi are famed feudal lords; once examined together, we cannot rest secure.
translations.idiomatic: ' Wu and Jiaoxi are famed among the princes. Once scrutinized together, neither of us can rest secure.

sentences.zh: 吳王身有內疾，不能朝請二十餘年，常患見疑，無以自白，脅肩累足，猶懼不見釋。

translations.literal: The King of Wu has internal illness and cannot attend court for more than twenty years; he constantly fears being suspected with no means to clear himself, shoulders hunched and feet piled, still afraid of not being released.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu has been too ill to attend court for more than twenty years. He lives in constant fear of suspicion with no way to clear himself—shoulders hunched, feet drawn in—still afraid he will not be spared.

sentences.zh: 竊聞大王以爵事有過。

translations.literal: I have privately heard that Your Majesty had fault in the matter of selling ranks.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard privately that Your Majesty was faulted in the matter of selling ranks.

sentences.zh: 所聞諸侯削地，罪不至此；

translations.literal: What I hear is that feudal lords' lands cut—the crime did not reach this;
translations.idiomatic: What I hear is that when feudal lords lose territory, the crime does not warrant this;

sentences.zh: 此恐不止削地而已。

translations.literal: this I fear is not only cutting territory.
translations.idiomatic: and I fear this will not stop at cutting territory alone.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「有之。

translations.literal: " The king said: "It is so.
translations.idiomatic: " The king said, "It is so.

sentences.zh: 子將奈何？

translations.literal: What will you do?
translations.idiomatic: What do you propose?

sentences.zh: 」高曰：「吳王自以與大王同憂，願因時循理，棄軀以除患於天下，意亦可乎？

translations.literal: " Gao said: "The King of Wu considers himself to share Your Majesty's worry; he wishes by the time and reason's course to cast aside his body to remove the affliction from all under Heaven—would that be acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: " Gao said, "The King of Wu believes he shares Your Majesty's peril. He wishes, seizing the moment and following right principle, to cast aside his body and remove this affliction from the realm. Would that be acceptable?

sentences.zh: 」膠西王瞿然駭曰：「寡人何敢如是！

translations.literal: " King Ying of Jiaoxi started in alarm and said: "How dare I do such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: " King Ying of Jiaoxi started in alarm. "How dare I do such a thing!

sentences.zh: 王上雖急，固有死耳，安得不事！

translations.literal: Though the Son of Heaven is harsh, there is certainly death—how could one not serve!
translations.idiomatic: However harsh the Son of Heaven may be, death is certain—how could one refuse to serve!

sentences.zh: 」高曰：「御史大夫晁錯，營惑天子，侵奪諸侯，朝廷疾怨，諸侯皆有背叛之意，人事極矣。

translations.literal: " Gao said: "Grandee Secretary Chao Cuo confuses the Son of Heaven and invades and seizes from feudal lords; court and ministers resent with illness, all feudal lords have intent to rebel—human affairs have reached the limit.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao said, "Grandee Secretary Chao Cuo bewilders the Son of Heaven and strips the feudal lords. Court and capital seethe with resentment; every prince harbors thoughts of rebellion. Human affairs have reached their limit.

sentences.zh: 彗星出，蝗蟲起，此萬世一時；

translations.literal: A comet has appeared, locusts have risen—this is an opportunity of ten thousand generations;
translations.idiomatic: A comet has appeared, locusts have risen—this is a chance that comes once in ten thousand generations;

sentences.zh: 而愁勞，聖人所以起也。

translations.literal: and worry and toil are why the sage arises.
translations.idiomatic: and worry and toil are what rouse the sage to act.

sentences.zh: 吳王內以晁錯為誅，外從大王后車，方洋天下，所向者降，所指者下，莫敢不服。

translations.literal: The King of Wu within will take Chao Cuo for execution; without will follow Your Majesty's rear carriage; far and wide across all under Heaven, where he turns all submit, where he points all fall—none dare not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu will execute Chao Cuo within the realm and follow Your Majesty's chariot without. He will sweep across the realm—where he turns, men submit; where he points, cities fall. None will dare refuse.

sentences.zh: 大王誠幸而許之一言，則吳王率楚王略函谷關，守滎陽、敖倉之粟，距漢兵，治次舍，須大王。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly deigns to assent with one word, then the King of Wu will lead the King of Chu to seize Hangu Pass, guard the grain at Xingyang and Aocang, resist Han troops, set up lodging, and wait for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will grant a single word of assent, the King of Wu will lead the King of Chu to seize Hangu Pass, hold the grain at Xingyang and Aocang, block Han's armies, and prepare lodging while he awaits Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 大王幸而臨之，則天下可並，兩主分割，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty deigns to come, then all under Heaven can be united, two lords dividing it—is that not also acceptable!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty comes in person, the realm can be united—or two lords can divide it. Would that not serve as well!

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「善！

translations.literal: " The king said: "Good!
translations.idiomatic: " The king said, "Good!

sentences.zh: 」歸，報吳王，吳王猶恐其不果，乃身自為使者，至膠西面約之。

translations.literal: " He returned and reported to the King of Wu; the King of Wu still feared it would not succeed and thereupon went in person as envoy to Jiaoxi's border to covenant with him.
translations.idiomatic: " He returned and reported to the King of Wu. The King of Wu still feared the plan would fail and went in person as envoy to Jiaoxi's border to seal the covenant.

sentences.zh: 膠西群臣或聞王謀，諫曰：「諸侯地不能當漢十二，為叛逆以憂太后，非計也。

translations.literal: Some of Jiaoxi's ministers heard the king's plot and remonstrated: "Feudal lords' lands cannot equal one-twelfth of Han; to rebel and worry the empress dowager is not a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Some of Jiaoxi's ministers heard the king's plot and remonstrated: "The feudal lords' lands cannot match one-twelfth of Han's. To rebel and grieve the empress dowager is no plan at all.

sentences.zh: 今承一帝，尚雲不易；

translations.literal: Now serving one emperor, it is still said not easy;
translations.idiomatic: Serving one emperor is already said to be hard enough;

sentences.zh: 假令事成，兩主分爭，患乃益生。

translations.literal: suppose it succeeds, two lords contend and afflictions will only increase.
translations.idiomatic: suppose it succeeds—two lords will contend, and troubles will only multiply.

sentences.zh: 」王不聽，遂發使約齊、菑川、膠東、濟南，皆許諾。

translations.literal: " The king did not listen and thereupon sent envoys to covenant with Qi, Zichuan, Jiaodong, and Jinan; all promised.
translations.idiomatic: " The king would not listen. He sent envoys to covenant with Qi, Zichuan, Jiaodong, and Jinan, and all promised.

sentences.zh: 初，楚元王好書，與魯申公、穆生、白生俱受《詩》於浮丘伯；

translations.literal: At the outset, King Yuan of Chu loved books; with Lu's Lord Shen, Mu Sheng, and Bai Sheng together he received the Odes from Fuqiu Bo;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, King Yuan of Chu loved learning. With Lord Shen of Lu, Mu Sheng, and Bai Sheng he studied the Odes under Fuqiu Bo;

sentences.zh: 及王楚，以三人為中大夫。

translations.literal: when he became king of Chu, he made the three men central grandees.
translations.idiomatic: when he became king of Chu he made all three central grandees.

sentences.zh: 穆生不耆酒；

translations.literal: Mu Sheng did not love wine;
translations.idiomatic: Mu Sheng did not drink wine;

sentences.zh: 元王每置酒，常為穆生設醴。

translations.literal: King Yuan each time he set out wine always set out sweet wine for Mu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: whenever King Yuan held a feast he always set out sweet wine for Mu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 及子夷王、孫王戊即位，常設，後乃忘設焉。

translations.literal: When his son King Yi and grandson King Wu took the throne, it was routinely set, but later they forgot to set it.
translations.idiomatic: When his son King Yi and grandson King Wu succeeded, the custom held for a time, but later they forgot to set it out.

sentences.zh: 穆生退，曰：「可以逝矣！

translations.literal: Mu Sheng withdrew, saying: "I may depart!
translations.idiomatic: Mu Sheng withdrew, saying, "It is time to go!

sentences.zh: 醴酒不設，王之意怠；

translations.literal: Sweet wine not set—the king's intent is slack;
translations.idiomatic: No sweet wine set out—the king's regard has slackened;

sentences.zh: 不去，楚人將鉗我於市。

translations.literal: if I do not leave, the men of Chu will clamp me in the market.
translations.idiomatic: if I do not leave, the men of Chu will clamp me in irons at the market.

sentences.zh: 」遂稱疾臥。

translations.literal: " He thereupon claimed illness and kept to bed.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon claimed illness and kept to his bed.

sentences.zh: 申公、白生強起之，曰：「獨不念先王之德與！

translations.literal: Lord Shen and Bai Sheng forcibly roused him, saying: "Will you alone not recall the former king's virtue!
translations.idiomatic: Lord Shen and Bai Sheng tried to rouse him by force, saying, "Will you alone forget the former king's kindness!

sentences.zh: 今王一旦失小禮，何足至此！

translations.literal: Now the king once lost a small courtesy—how does it reach this!
translations.idiomatic: The present king missed one small courtesy—how can that justify this!

sentences.zh: 」穆生曰：「《易》稱：『知幾其神乎！

translations.literal: " Mu Sheng said: "The Changes says: 'To know the subtle—is it not spiritlike!
translations.idiomatic: " Mu Sheng said, "The Changes says, 'To know the subtle—is that not spiritlike!

sentences.zh: 幾者，動之微，吉兇之先見者也。

translations.literal: The subtle is the incipient of movement, fortune and calamity seen beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: The subtle is the first stir of movement, fortune and calamity seen before they arrive.

sentences.zh: 君子見幾而作，不俟終日。

translations.literal: The noble person seeing the subtle acts; he does not wait out the day.
translations.idiomatic: The noble person sees the subtle and acts; he does not wait out the day.

sentences.zh: 』先王之所以禮吾三人者，為道存也。

translations.literal: ' The former king's reason for honoring us three was that the Way endured.
translations.idiomatic: ' The former king honored us three because the Way still endured.

sentences.zh: 今而忽之，是忘道也。

translations.literal: Now to slight us—this is forgetting the Way.
translations.idiomatic: To slight us now is to forget the Way.

sentences.zh: 忘道之人，胡可與久處，豈為區區之禮哉！

translations.literal: One who forgets the Way—how can one dwell long with him; how is it for a trifling courtesy!
translations.idiomatic: How can one dwell long with one who has forgotten the Way—for a trifling courtesy!

sentences.zh: 」遂謝病去。

translations.literal: " He thereupon took leave for illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " He took leave on grounds of illness and departed.

sentences.zh: 申公、白生獨留。

translations.literal: Lord Shen and Bai Sheng alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Shen and Bai Sheng alone remained.

sentences.zh: 王戊稍淫暴，太傅韋孟作詩諷諫，不聽，亦去，居於鄒。

translations.literal: King Wu gradually grew licentious and violent; Grand Tutor Wei Meng composed verse to admonish indirectly; he was not heeded and also left, dwelling in Zou.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu grew gradually licentious and violent. Grand Tutor Wei Meng wrote verse to admonish him indirectly; when the king would not listen, he too departed and lived in Zou.

sentences.zh: 戊因坐削地事，遂與吳通謀。

translations.literal: Wu on account of the matter of cut territory thereupon communicated plots with Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, implicated in the reduction of his territory, thereupon joined plots with the King of Wu.

sentences.zh: 申公、白生諫戊，戊胥靡之，衣之赭衣，使雅舂於市。

translations.literal: Lord Shen and Bai Sheng remonstrated with Wu; Wu made them bondsmen, clothed them in ochre garments, and made them pound grain with the mortar at the market.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Shen and Bai Sheng remonstrated with Wu. Wu made them convict bondsmen, clothed them in ochre, and set them pounding grain with the mortar in the market.

sentences.zh: 休侯富使人諫王。

translations.literal: Marquis Xiu Fu sent someone to remonstrate with the king.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Xiu Fu sent someone to remonstrate with the king.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「季父不吾與，我起，先取季父矣！

translations.literal: The king said: "My uncle does not stand with me; when I rise, I will take my uncle first!
translations.idiomatic: The king said, "My uncle will not stand with me. When I rise, I will take my uncle first!

sentences.zh: 」休侯懼，乃與母太夫人奔京師。

translations.literal: " Marquis Xiu was afraid and thereupon with his mother the great lady fled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " Marquis Xiu was afraid and fled with his mother the great lady to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及削吳會稽、豫章郡書至，吳王遂先起兵，誅漢吏二千石以下；

translations.literal: When the document cutting Wu's Kuaiji and Yuzhang commanderies arrived, the King of Wu thereupon first raised troops and executed Han officials of two thousand piculs and below;
translations.idiomatic: When the edict cutting Kuaiji and Yuzhang from Wu arrived, the King of Wu was first to raise troops and execute Han officials of two thousand piculs rank and below;

sentences.zh: 膠西、膠東、菑川、濟南、楚、趙亦皆反。

translations.literal: Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Zichuan, Jinan, Chu, and Zhao also all rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Zichuan, Jinan, Chu, and Zhao rebelled as well.

sentences.zh: 楚相張尚、太傅趙夷吾諫王戊，戊殺尚、夷吾。

translations.literal: Chu's chancellor Zhang Shang and grand tutor Zhao Yiwu remonstrated with King Wu; Wu killed Shang and Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Chu's chancellor Zhang Shang and grand tutor Zhao Yiwu remonstrated with King Wu; Wu killed them both.

sentences.zh: 趙相建德、內史王悍諫王遂，遂燒殺建德、悍。

translations.literal: Zhao's chancellor Jian De and internuncius Wang Han remonstrated with King Sui; Sui burned them alive and killed Jian De and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's chancellor Jian De and internuncius Wang Han remonstrated with King Sui; Sui burned them alive.

sentences.zh: 齊王後悔，背約城守。

translations.literal: The King of Qi repented, broke the agreement, and held the city in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qi repented, broke the agreement, and defended the city.

sentences.zh: 濟北王城壞未完，其郎中令劫守，王不得發兵。

translations.literal: The King of Jibei's city walls were breached and not yet repaired; his Director of the Secretariat seized the garrison, and the king could not dispatch troops.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Jibei's walls were breached and not yet repaired; his Director of the Secretariat seized the garrison, and the king could not raise troops.

sentences.zh: 膠西王、膠東王為渠率，與菑川、濟南共攻齊，圍臨菑。

translations.literal: The Kings of Jiaoxi and Jiaodong served as ringleaders, and together with Zichuan and Jinan attacked Qi and besieged Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: The Kings of Jiaoxi and Jiaodong led the attack, and together with Zichuan and Jinan they assaulted Qi and besieged Linzi.

sentences.zh: 趙王遂發兵住其西界，欲待吳、楚俱進，北使匈奴與連兵。

translations.literal: The King of Zhao thereupon raised troops and halted on its western border, wishing to wait until Wu and Chu advanced together and to send north to the Xiongnu to join forces.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Zhao thereupon raised troops and held the western border, intending to wait for Wu and Chu to advance together and to link arms with the Xiongnu in the north.

sentences.zh: 吳王悉其士卒，下令國中曰：「寡人年六十二，身自將；

translations.literal: The King of Wu mustered all his troops and ordered within the state, saying: "I am sixty-two years old and shall command in person;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu mustered all his troops and proclaimed throughout the state, "I am sixty-two years old and shall take command in person;

sentences.zh: 少子年十四，亦為士卒先。

translations.literal: My youngest son is fourteen and shall also lead the troops as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: My youngest son is fourteen and shall also lead the troops as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 諸年上與寡人同，下與少子等，皆發。

translations.literal: All from my age upward and from my youngest son's age downward—everyone shall be mobilized.
translations.idiomatic: All from my age upward and from my youngest son's age downward shall be mobilized.

sentences.zh: 」凡二十餘萬人。

translations.literal: " In all there were more than two hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: " In all there were more than two hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 南使閩、東越，閩、東越亦發兵從。

translations.literal: He sent south to Min and Dongyue, and Min and Dongyue also raised troops to follow.
translations.idiomatic: He sent south to Min and Dongyue, and they too raised troops to follow.

sentences.zh: 吳王起兵於廣陵，西涉淮，因並楚兵，發使遺諸侯書，罪狀晁錯，欲合兵誅之。

translations.literal: The King of Wu raised troops at Guangling, crossed west over the Huai, and thereupon merged Chu forces; he sent envoys with letters to the feudal lords, listing Chao Cuo's crimes, wishing to unite armies and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu raised troops at Guangling, crossed the Huai westward, merged Chu forces, and sent envoys with letters to the feudal lords listing Chao Cuo's crimes, intending to unite armies and kill him.

sentences.zh: 吳、楚共攻梁，破棘壁，殺數萬人；

translations.literal: Wu and Chu together attacked Liang, broke through Jibi, and killed tens of thousands;
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Chu together attacked Liang, broke through Jibi, and killed tens of thousands;

sentences.zh: 乘勝而前，銳甚。

translations.literal: pressing the victory forward, they were very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: pressing their victory forward, they were very fierce.

sentences.zh: 梁孝王遣將軍擊之，又敗梁兩軍，士卒皆還走。

translations.literal: King Xiao of Liang sent generals to strike them, but they again defeated Liang's two armies, and the soldiers all fled back.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiao of Liang sent generals against them, but they again defeated Liang's two armies, and the troops all fled.

sentences.zh: 梁王城守睢陽。

translations.literal: The King of Liang held Suiyang in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Liang defended Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝且崩，戒太子曰：「即有緩急，周亞夫真可任將兵。

translations.literal: At the outset, when Emperor Wen was about to die, he warned the crown prince, saying: "If there should be urgency, Zhou Yafu truly can be entrusted with commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Wen was about to die, he warned the crown prince, "If there is an emergency, Zhou Yafu truly can be entrusted with command of the army.

sentences.zh: 」及七國反書聞，上乃拜中尉周亞夫為太尉，將三十六將軍往擊吳、楚，遣曲周侯酈寄擊趙，將軍欒布擊齊；

translations.literal: " When word of the Seven States' rebellion arrived, the emperor thereupon appointed Commandant of the Guards Zhou Yafu Grand Commandant, to lead thirty-six generals to strike Wu and Chu; he sent Marquis Ji of Quzhou Li Ji to strike Zhao and General Luan Bu to strike Qi;
translations.idiomatic: " When word of the Seven States' rebellion arrived, the emperor appointed Commandant of the Guards Zhou Yafu Grand Commandant and sent him with thirty-six generals against Wu and Chu; he sent Marquis Ji of Quzhou Li Ji against Zhao and General Luan Bu against Qi;

sentences.zh: 復召竇嬰，拜為大將軍，使屯滎陽監齊、趙兵。

translations.literal: He again summoned Dou Ying, appointed him Grand General, and had him garrison at Xingyang to oversee Qi and Zhao forces.
translations.idiomatic: He again summoned Dou Ying, appointed him Grand General, and stationed him at Xingyang to oversee the Qi and Zhao armies.

sentences.zh: 初，晁錯所更令三十章，諸侯讙嘩。

translations.literal: At the outset, the thirty chapters of ordinances that Chao Cuo had revised made the feudal lords clamor in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the thirty chapters of ordinances that Chao Cuo had revised threw the feudal lords into an uproar.

sentences.zh: 錯父聞之，從穎川來，謂錯曰：「上初即位，公為政用事，侵削諸侯，疏人骨肉，口語多怨，公何為也？

translations.literal: Cuo's father heard of it, came from Yingchuan, and said to Cuo: "The emperor has just taken the throne; you hold power in government, encroach upon and pare the feudal lords, estrange men of flesh and bone, and many murmur in resentment—what are you doing?
translations.idiomatic: Cuo's father heard of it, came from Yingchuan, and said to Cuo, "The emperor has just taken the throne; you hold power, encroach upon and pare the feudal lords, estrange kin, and many murmur in resentment—what are you doing?

sentences.zh: 」錯曰：「固也。

translations.literal: " Cuo said: "Indeed.
translations.idiomatic: " Cuo said, "Indeed.

sentences.zh: 不如此，天子不尊，宗廟不安。

translations.literal: If it were not so, the Son of Heaven would not be honored and the ancestral temple would not be secure.
translations.idiomatic: If it were not so, the Son of Heaven would not be honored and the ancestral temple would not be secure.

sentences.zh: 」父曰：「劉氏安矣而晁氏危，吾去公歸矣！

translations.literal: " His father said: "The Liu clan will be secure but the Chao clan will be in peril—I leave you and return home!
translations.idiomatic: " His father said, "The Liu clan will be secure but the Chao clan will be in peril—I leave you and go home!

sentences.zh: 」遂飲藥死，曰：「吾不忍見禍逮身！

translations.literal: " Thereupon he drank poison and died, saying: "I cannot bear to see disaster reach my person!
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he drank poison and died, saying, "I cannot bear to see disaster reach me!

sentences.zh: 」後十餘日，吳、楚七國俱反，以誅錯為名。

translations.literal: " More than ten days later, Wu, Chu, and the Seven States all rebelled, taking the execution of Cuo as their pretext.
translations.idiomatic: " More than ten days later, Wu, Chu, and the Seven States all rebelled, taking the execution of Cuo as their pretext.

sentences.zh: 上與錯議出軍事，錯欲令上自將兵而身居守；

translations.literal: The emperor discussed military affairs with Cuo; Cuo wished to have the emperor lead the army in person while he himself remained to guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor discussed military affairs with Cuo; Cuo wished to have the emperor lead the army in person while he himself remained behind to guard the capital;

sentences.zh: 又言：「徐、僮之旁吳所未下者，可以予吳。

translations.literal: He also said: "The lands beside Xu and Tong that Wu has not yet taken may be granted to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: he also said, "The lands beside Xu and Tong that Wu has not yet taken may be granted to Wu.

sentences.zh: 」錯素與吳相袁盎不善，錯所居坐，盎輒避；

translations.literal: " Cuo had long been on bad terms with Wu's chancellor Yuan Ang; wherever Cuo sat, Ang would avoid it;
translations.idiomatic: " Cuo had long been on bad terms with Wu's chancellor Yuan Ang; wherever Cuo sat, Ang would avoid it;

sentences.zh: 盎所居坐，錯亦避；

translations.literal: wherever Ang sat, Cuo also avoided it;
translations.idiomatic: wherever Ang sat, Cuo also avoided it;

sentences.zh: 兩人未嘗同堂語。

translations.literal: the two had never spoken in the same hall.
translations.idiomatic: the two had never spoken in the same hall.

sentences.zh: 及錯為御史大夫，使吏按盎受吳王財物，抵罪；

translations.literal: When Cuo became Grand Secretary, he sent officials to investigate Ang for receiving goods from the King of Wu and convicted him;
translations.idiomatic: When Cuo became Grand Secretary, he sent officials to investigate Ang for receiving goods from the King of Wu and convicted him;

sentences.zh: 詔赦以為庶人。

translations.literal: an edict pardoned him and made him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: an edict pardoned him and reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 吳、楚反，錯謂丞、史曰：「袁盎多受吳王金錢，專為蔽匿，言不反；

translations.literal: When Wu and Chu rebelled, Cuo said to the aides and clerks: "Yuan Ang received much gold from the King of Wu, deliberately concealed it, and said they would not rebel;
translations.idiomatic: When Wu and Chu rebelled, Cuo said to the aides and clerks, "Yuan Ang received much gold from the King of Wu, deliberately concealed it, and said they would not rebel;

sentences.zh: 今果反，欲請治盎，宜知其計謀。

translations.literal: now they have indeed rebelled—I wish to request that Ang be prosecuted; he ought to know their plans.
translations.idiomatic: now they have indeed rebelled—I wish to prosecute Ang; he ought to know their plans.

sentences.zh: 」丞、史曰：「事未發，治之有絕；

translations.literal: " The aides and clerks said: "Before the affair broke out, prosecuting him would have cut off relations;
translations.idiomatic: " The aides and clerks said, "Before the affair broke out, prosecuting him would have cut off relations;

sentences.zh: 今兵西向，治之何益！

translations.literal: now the armies face west—what good is prosecuting him!
translations.idiomatic: now the armies face west—what good is prosecuting him!

sentences.zh: 且盎不宜有謀。

translations.literal: Moreover Ang is not likely to have plotted.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Ang is unlikely to have plotted.

sentences.zh: 」錯猶與未決。

translations.literal: " Cuo still hesitated and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: " Cuo still hesitated and had not decided.

sentences.zh: 人有告盎，盎恐，夜見竇嬰，為言吳所以反，願至前，口對狀。

translations.literal: Someone informed Ang; Ang was afraid and by night visited Dou Ying, explaining why Wu had rebelled and wishing to go before the throne and answer face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Someone informed Ang; Ang was afraid and visited Dou Ying by night, explained why Wu had rebelled, and asked to go before the throne and answer in person.

sentences.zh: 嬰入言，上乃召盎。

translations.literal: Ying entered and spoke; the emperor thereupon summoned Ang.
translations.idiomatic: Ying reported this, and the emperor summoned Ang.

sentences.zh: 盎入見，上方與錯調兵食。

translations.literal: Ang entered to audience; the emperor was just then with Cuo arranging troops and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Ang entered to audience; the emperor was just then with Cuo arranging troops and provisions.

sentences.zh: 上問盎：「今吳、楚反，於公意何如？

translations.literal: The emperor asked Ang: "Now that Wu and Chu have rebelled, what is your view?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Ang, "Now that Wu and Chu have rebelled, what is your view?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「不足憂也！

translations.literal: " He replied: "Nothing to worry about!
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Nothing to worry about!

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「吳王即山鑄錢，煮海為鹽，誘天豪傑；

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "The King of Wu coins money from his mountains, boils the sea for salt, and lures heaven's great heroes;
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The King of Wu coins money from his mountains, boils the sea for salt, and lures the realm's great heroes;

sentences.zh: 白頭舉事、此其計不百全，豈發乎！

translations.literal: he raises the affair with white hair—this plan is not a hundred parts secure; how could he have launched it!
translations.idiomatic: he raises the affair in his old age—this plan is not fully secure; how could he have launched it!

sentences.zh: 何以言其無能為也？

translations.literal: Why do you say he cannot accomplish anything?
translations.idiomatic: Why do you say he cannot accomplish anything?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「吳銅鹽之利則有之，安得豪傑而誘之！

translations.literal: " He replied: "Wu has the profit of copper and salt, but how could there be heroes to lure!
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Wu has the profit of copper and salt, but where are the heroes to lure!

sentences.zh: 誠令吳得豪傑，亦且輔而為誼，不反矣。

translations.literal: If Wu truly obtained heroes, they would also assist him in righteousness and would not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: If Wu truly obtained heroes, they would assist him in loyalty and would not rebel.

sentences.zh: 吳所誘皆亡賴子弟、亡命、鑄錢奸人，故相誘以亂」錯曰：「盎策之善。

translations.literal: Those whom Wu lures are all worthless scions, fugitives, and coiners and villains—therefore they lure one another to rebellion." Cuo said: "Ang's assessment is good.
translations.idiomatic: Those whom Wu lures are all worthless scions, fugitives, and coiners and villains—therefore they lure one another to rebellion." Cuo said, "Ang's assessment is good.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「計安出？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Where does the plan come from?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Where does the plan come from?

sentences.zh: 」盎對曰：「願屏左右。

translations.literal: " Ang replied: "I wish to dismiss those at hand.
translations.idiomatic: " Ang replied, "I wish to dismiss those at hand.

sentences.zh: 」上屏人，獨錯在。

translations.literal: " The emperor dismissed the attendants; only Cuo remained.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor dismissed the attendants; only Cuo remained.

sentences.zh: 盎曰：「臣所言，人臣不得知。

translations.literal: Ang said: "What your servant will say must not be known to other ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Ang said, "What your servant will say must not be known to other ministers.

sentences.zh: 」乃屏錯。

translations.literal: " He then had Cuo dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " He then had Cuo dismissed.

sentences.zh: 錯趨避東廂，甚恨。

translations.literal: Cuo hurried to avoid him in the east wing, full of hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Cuo hurried off to the east wing, full of hatred.

sentences.zh: 上卒問盎，對曰：「吳、楚相遺書，言高皇帝王子弟各有分地，今賊臣晁錯擅適諸侯，削奪之地，以故反，欲西共誅錯，復故地而罷。

translations.literal: The emperor at last questioned Ang; he replied: "Wu and Chu sent each other letters saying that Emperor Gao's imperial sons and younger brothers each had allotted lands, but now the traitor minister Chao Cuo on his own authority punished the feudal lords and seized their lands—therefore they rebel, wishing to march west together to execute Cuo, restore their old lands, and then disband.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at last questioned Ang; he replied, "Wu and Chu sent each other letters saying that Emperor Gao's imperial sons and younger brothers each had allotted lands, but now the traitor minister Chao Cuo on his own authority punished the feudal lords and seized their lands—therefore they rebel, wishing to march west together to execute Cuo, restore their old lands, and then disband.

sentences.zh: 方今計獨有斬錯，發使赦吳、楚七國，復其故地，則兵可毋血刃而俱罷。

translations.literal: At present the plan is solely to behead Cuo, send envoys to pardon Wu, Chu, and the Seven States, and restore their old lands—then the armies can all disband without a blade being bloodied.
translations.idiomatic: At present the only plan is to behead Cuo, send envoys to pardon Wu, Chu, and the Seven States, and restore their old lands—then the armies can all disband without bloodshed.

sentences.zh: 」於是上默然良久，曰：「顧誠何如？

translations.literal: " Thereupon the emperor was silent a long while and said: "But if it is truly so?
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the emperor was silent a long while and said, "But if it is truly so?

sentences.zh: 吾不愛一人以謝天下。

translations.literal: I do not begrudge one man to appease all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I do not begrudge one man to appease all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」盎曰：「愚計出此，唯上孰計之！

translations.literal: " Ang said: "This foolish plan comes to this—may Your Majesty weigh it carefully!
translations.idiomatic: " Ang said, "This foolish plan comes to this—may Your Majesty weigh it carefully!

sentences.zh: 」乃拜盎為太常，密裝治行。

translations.literal: " He thereupon appointed Ang Grand Master of Ceremonies and secretly prepared his journey.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon appointed Ang Grand Master of Ceremonies and secretly prepared his journey.

sentences.zh: 後十餘日，上令丞相青、中尉嘉、廷尉歐劾奏錯：「不稱主上德信，欲疏群臣、百姓，又欲以城邑予吳，無臣子禮，大逆無道。

translations.literal: More than ten days later, the emperor ordered Chancellor Qing, Commandant of the Guards Jia, and Commandant of Justice Ou to impeach and memorialize against Cuo: "He does not proclaim the ruler's virtue and trustworthiness, wishes to estrange ministers and the people, and also wishes to grant cities to Wu—lacking the rites of minister and son, he is greatly rebellious and without the Way.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten days later, the emperor ordered Chancellor Qing, Commandant of the Guards Jia, and Commandant of Justice Ou to impeach Cuo: "He does not proclaim the ruler's virtue and trustworthiness, wishes to estrange ministers and the people, and also wishes to grant cities to Wu—lacking the rites of minister and son, he is greatly rebellious and without the Way.

sentences.zh: 錯當要斬，父母、妻子、同產無少長皆棄市。

translations.literal: Cuo should be decapitated at the waist; parents, wife, children, and siblings of the same womb, none young or old, should all be executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Cuo should be decapitated at the waist; parents, wife, children, and siblings, none young or old, should all be executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 」制曰：「可。

translations.literal: " The rescript said: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The rescript said, "Approved.

sentences.zh: 」錯殊不知。

translations.literal: " Cuo knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: " Cuo knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 壬子，上使中尉召錯，紿載行市，錯衣朝衣斬東市。

translations.literal: On renzi, the emperor sent the Commandant of the Guards to summon Cuo, deceived him into a carriage, and paraded him through the market; Cuo, in court robes, was beheaded in the eastern market.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, the emperor sent the Commandant of the Guards to summon Cuo, tricked him into a carriage, and paraded him through the market; Cuo, in court robes, was beheaded in the eastern market.

sentences.zh: 上乃使袁盎與吳王弟子宗正德侯通使吳。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent Yuan Ang and the King of Wu's younger kinsman, Director of the Imperial Clan De Marquis Tong, as envoys to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Yuan Ang and the King of Wu's younger kinsman, Director of the Imperial Clan De Marquis Tong, as envoys to Wu.

sentences.zh: 謁者僕射鄧公為校尉，上書言軍事，見上，上問曰：「道軍所來，聞晁錯死，吳、楚罷不？

translations.literal: Master of Ceremonies Deng Gong served as colonel; he submitted a memorial on military affairs, saw the emperor, and the emperor asked: "Coming from the army's route, I have heard Chao Cuo is dead—have Wu and Chu disbanded?
translations.idiomatic: Master of Ceremonies Deng Gong served as colonel; he submitted a memorial on military affairs and saw the emperor, who asked, "Coming from the army's route, I have heard Chao Cuo is dead—have Wu and Chu disbanded?

sentences.zh: 」鄧公曰：「吳為反數十歲矣；

translations.literal: " Deng Gong said: "Wu has been preparing rebellion for decades;
translations.idiomatic: " Deng Gong said, "Wu has been preparing rebellion for decades;

sentences.zh: 發怒削地，以誅錯為名，其意不在錯也。

translations.literal: angered by the paring of their lands, they take the execution of Cuo as their pretext—their intent is not on Cuo.
translations.idiomatic: angered by the paring of their lands, they take the execution of Cuo as their pretext—their intent is not on Cuo.

sentences.zh: 且臣恐天下之士拑口不敢復言矣。

translations.literal: Moreover your servant fears that gentlemen throughout the realm will clamp their mouths shut and not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover your servant fears that gentlemen throughout the realm will clamp their mouths shut and not dare speak again.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「何哉？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "How so?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "How so?

sentences.zh: 」鄧公曰：「夫晁錯患諸侯強大不可制，故請削之以尊京師，萬世之利也。

translations.literal: " Deng Gong said: "Chao Cuo feared that the feudal lords were strong and could not be controlled, and therefore requested to pare them to honor the capital region—benefit for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: " Deng Gong said, "Chao Cuo feared that the feudal lords were strong and could not be controlled, and therefore requested to pare them to honor the capital—a benefit for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 計畫始行，卒受大戮。

translations.literal: The plan had barely begun when he suddenly suffered great execution.
translations.idiomatic: The plan had barely begun when he suddenly suffered execution.

sentences.zh: 內杜忠臣之口，外為諸侯報仇，臣竊為陛下不取也。

translations.literal: Within, the mouths of loyal ministers are stopped; without, revenge is wrought for the feudal lords—your servant ventures to think Your Majesty should not have taken this course.
translations.idiomatic: Within, the mouths of loyal ministers are stopped; without, revenge is wrought for the feudal lords—your servant ventures to think Your Majesty should not have taken this course.

sentences.zh: 」於是帝喟然長息曰：「公言善，吾亦恨之！

translations.literal: " Thereupon the emperor sighed long and said: "Your words are good—I too regret it!
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the emperor sighed long and said, "Your words are good—I too regret it!

sentences.zh: 袁盎、劉通至吳，吳、楚兵已攻梁壁矣。

translations.literal: Yuan Ang and Liu Tong reached Wu; Wu and Chu troops had already attacked Liang's walls.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ang and Liu Tong reached Wu; Wu and Chu troops had already attacked Liang's walls.

sentences.zh: 宗正以親故，先入見，諭吳王，令拜受詔。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Clan, by reason of kinship, entered first to audience, instructed the King of Wu, and ordered him to bow and receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Clan, by reason of kinship, entered first, instructed the King of Wu, and ordered him to bow and receive the edict.

sentences.zh: 吳王聞袁盎來，知其欲說，笑而應曰：「我已為東帝，尚誰拜！

translations.literal: The King of Wu heard Yuan Ang had come, knew he wished to persuade him, laughed and replied: "I am already Eastern Emperor—whom else should I bow to!
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu heard Yuan Ang had come, knew he wished to persuade him, laughed and replied, "I am already Eastern Emperor—whom else should I bow to!

sentences.zh: 」不肯見盎，而留軍中，欲劫使將；

translations.literal: " He refused to see Ang but detained him in the army, wishing to coerce him into commanding;
translations.idiomatic: " He refused to see Ang but detained him in the army, wishing to coerce him into taking command;

sentences.zh: 盎不肯，使人圍守，且殺之。

translations.literal: Ang refused; they sent men to surround and guard him and were about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Ang refused; they sent men to surround and guard him and were about to kill him.

sentences.zh: 盎得間，脫亡歸報。

translations.literal: Ang found an opening, escaped, and returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: Ang found an opening, escaped, and returned to report.

sentences.zh: 太尉亞夫言於上曰：「楚兵剽輕，難與爭鋒，願以梁委之，絕其食道，乃可制也。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yafu spoke to the emperor, saying: "Chu troops are swift and light—hard to contend with at the spearhead; I wish to yield Liang to them, cut off their supply routes, and only then can they be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yafu spoke to the emperor, saying, "Chu troops are swift and light—hard to meet head-on; I wish to yield Liang to them, cut off their supply routes, and only then can they be controlled.

sentences.zh: 」上許之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 亞夫乘六乘傳，將會兵滎陽。

translations.literal: Yafu rode the six-relay post and was about to assemble troops at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yafu took the six-relay post and was about to assemble troops at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 發至霸上，趙涉庶說亞夫曰：「吳王素富，懷輯死士久矣。

translations.literal: When he set out and reached Bashang, Zhao She the commoner advised Yafu, saying: "The King of Wu has long been rich and for years has cherished and gathered men who would die for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he set out and reached Bashang, Zhao She the commoner advised Yafu, saying, "The King of Wu has long been rich and for years has gathered men who would die for him.

sentences.zh: 此知將軍且行，必置間人於殽、澠厄狹之間；

translations.literal: He knows the general is about to march and is sure to place spies in the narrow passes of Yao and Mian;
translations.idiomatic: He knows the general is about to march and is sure to place spies in the narrow passes of Yao and Mian;

sentences.zh: 且兵事上神密，將軍何不從此右去，走藍田，出武關，抵洛陽！

translations.literal: moreover military affairs above all require secrecy—why does the general not turn right from here, hurry through Lantian, exit Wu Pass, and reach Luoyang!
translations.idiomatic: moreover military affairs above all require secrecy—why does the general not turn right from here, hurry through Lantian, exit Wu Pass, and reach Luoyang!

sentences.zh: 間不過差一二日，直入武庫，擊鳴鼓。

translations.literal: The delay would be no more than a day or two off; enter straight into the Arsenal and strike the sounding drum.
translations.idiomatic: The delay would be no more than a day or two; enter straight into the Arsenal and strike the sounding drum.

sentences.zh: 諸侯聞之，以為將軍從天而下也。

translations.literal: The feudal lords hearing it would think the general had descended from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The feudal lords hearing it would think the general had descended from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」太尉如其計，至洛陽，喜曰：「七國反，吾乘傳至此，不自意全。

translations.literal: " The Grand Commandant followed his plan; when he reached Luoyang he rejoiced, saying: "The Seven States rebelled—I rode the relay post to here and did not expect to arrive whole.
translations.idiomatic: " The Grand Commandant followed his plan; when he reached Luoyang he rejoiced, saying, "The Seven States rebelled—I rode the relay post here and did not expect to arrive safe.

sentences.zh: 今吾據滎陽，滎陽以東，無足憂者。

translations.literal: Now that I hold Xingyang, east of Xingyang there is nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I hold Xingyang, east of Xingyang there is nothing to worry about.

sentences.zh: 」使吏搜殽、澠間，果得吳伏兵。

translations.literal: " He sent officials to search between Yao and Mian and indeed found Wu's ambush troops.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent officials to search between Yao and Mian and indeed found Wu's ambush troops.

sentences.zh: 乃請趙涉為護軍。

translations.literal: He thereupon requested Zhao She as Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon requested Zhao She as Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 太尉引兵東北走昌邑。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant led his army northeast toward Changyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant led his army northeast toward Changyi.

sentences.zh: 吳攻梁急，梁數使使條侯求救，條侯不許。

translations.literal: Wu pressed the attack on Liang hard; Liang repeatedly sent envoys to Marquis of Tiao begging rescue, and Marquis of Tiao would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Wu pressed the attack on Liang hard; Liang repeatedly sent envoys to Marquis of Tiao begging rescue, and Marquis of Tiao would not agree.

sentences.zh: 又使使訴條侯於上。

translations.literal: He again sent envoys to appeal against Marquis of Tiao to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent envoys to appeal to the emperor against Marquis of Tiao.

sentences.zh: 上使告條侯救梁，亞夫不奉詔，堅壁不出；

translations.literal: The emperor sent word telling Marquis of Tiao to rescue Liang; Yafu did not obey the edict and held his walls firm without coming out;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent word telling Marquis of Tiao to rescue Liang; Yafu did not obey the edict and held his walls firm without coming out;

sentences.zh: 而使弓高侯等將輕騎兵出淮泗口，絕吳、楚兵後，塞其饟道。

translations.literal: instead he had Marquis of Gonggao and others lead light cavalry out from the Huai-Si mouth, cut off Wu and Chu forces in the rear, and block their supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: instead he had Marquis of Gonggao and others lead light cavalry out from the Huai-Si mouth, cut off Wu and Chu in the rear, and block their supply routes.

sentences.zh: 梁使中大夫韓安國及楚相尚弟羽為將軍；

translations.literal: Liang appointed Palace Grandee Han Anguo and Chu's chancellor Shang, younger brother Yu, as generals;
translations.idiomatic: Liang appointed Palace Grandee Han Anguo and Chu's chancellor Shang, younger brother Yu, as generals;

sentences.zh: 羽力戰，安國持重，乃得頗敗吳兵。

translations.literal: Yu fought with force, Anguo held steady, and only then were they able to defeat Wu troops considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Yu fought fiercely, Anguo held steady, and only then were they able to defeat Wu troops considerably.

sentences.zh: 吳兵欲西，梁城守，不敢西；

translations.literal: The Wu army wished to go west; Liang held cities in defense and did not dare go west;
translations.idiomatic: The Wu army wished to advance west; Liang defended its cities and they did not dare advance west;

sentences.zh: 即走條侯軍，會下邑，欲戰。

translations.literal: they thereupon ran to Marquis of Tiao's army, joined at Xiayi, and wished to fight.
translations.idiomatic: they thereupon fled to Marquis of Tiao's army, joined him at Xiayi, and wished to give battle.

sentences.zh: 條侯堅壁不肯戰；

translations.literal: Marquis of Tiao held his walls firm and would not fight;
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Tiao held his walls firm and would not fight;

sentences.zh: 吳糧絕卒饑，數挑戰，終不出，條侯軍中夜驚，內相攻擊，擾亂至帳下，亞夫堅臥不起，頃之，復定。

translations.literal: Wu's provisions were cut off and soldiers starved; they repeatedly provoked battle, yet he never came out; at night Marquis of Tiao's army was alarmed, men attacking one another within, disturbance reaching the commander's tent; Yafu lay firm and would not rise; in a moment all was settled again.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's supplies were cut off and the troops starved; they repeatedly challenged him to battle, yet he never came out; at night Marquis of Tiao's army was thrown into alarm, with men attacking one another within, and the disturbance reached the commander's tent; Yafu lay firm and would not rise; in a moment all was settled again.

sentences.zh: 吳奔壁東南陬，亞夫使備西北；

translations.literal: Wu fled to the southeast corner of the fortification; Yafu sent troops to guard the northwest;
translations.idiomatic: Wu fled to the southeast corner of the fortification; Yafu sent troops to guard the northwest;

sentences.zh: 已而其精兵果奔西北，不得入。

translations.literal: Before long their crack troops indeed rushed northwest and could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Before long their crack troops indeed rushed northwest and could not break in.

sentences.zh: 吳、楚士卒多饑死叛散，乃引而去。

translations.literal: Wu and Chu soldiers mostly starved, died, rebelled, and scattered; they then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Chu soldiers mostly starved, died, deserted, and scattered; they then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 二月，亞夫出精兵追擊，大破之。

translations.literal: In the second month Yafu sent out crack troops in pursuit and thoroughly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Yafu sent crack troops in pursuit and routed them.

sentences.zh: 吳王濞棄其軍，與壯士數千人夜亡走；

translations.literal: King of Wu Liu Pi abandoned his army and with several thousand stalwart men fled by night;
translations.idiomatic: King of Wu Liu Pi abandoned his army and fled by night with several thousand stalwart men;

sentences.zh: 楚王戊自殺。

translations.literal: King of Chu Liu Wu killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: King of Chu Liu Wu killed himself.

sentences.zh: 吳王之初發也，吳臣田祿伯為大將軍。

translations.literal: When the King of Wu first set out, Wu minister Tian Lubo was Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Wu first set out, the Wu minister Tian Lubo served as Grand General.

sentences.zh: 田祿伯曰：「兵屯聚而西，無它奇道，難以立功。

translations.literal: Tian Lubo said: "If troops mass and go west, with no other surprising route, it is hard to establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lubo said, "If troops mass and march west, with no other surprising route, it is hard to win merit.

sentences.zh: 臣願得五萬人，別循江、淮而上，收淮南、長沙，入武關，與大王會，此亦一奇也。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to obtain fifty thousand men, separately follow the Yangzi and Huai upstream, gather Huainan and Changsha, enter Wuguan, and meet with the great king—this is also one stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant asks for fifty thousand men to march separately up the Yangzi and Huai, take Huainan and Changsha, enter Wuguan, and join Your Majesty—this too would be a bold stroke.

sentences.zh: 」吳王太子諫曰：「王以反為名，此兵難以借人，人亦且反王，奈何？

translations.literal: " The crown prince of Wu remonstrated: "The king takes rebellion as his name; these troops are hard to lend to others, and others would also turn against the king—what then?
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince of Wu remonstrated, "You take rebellion as your cause; these troops cannot be lent to others, and others would turn against you as well—what then?

sentences.zh: 且擅兵而別，多它利害，徒自損耳！

translations.literal: Moreover to take troops on one's own authority and separate brings many other harms and benefits—merely self-damage!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to take troops on your own authority and march separately invites all manner of trouble—nothing but harm to yourself!

sentences.zh: 」吳王即不許田祿伯。

translations.literal: " The King of Wu then did not permit Tian Lubo.
translations.idiomatic: " The King of Wu then refused Tian Lubo.

sentences.zh: 吳少將桓將軍說王曰：「吳多步兵，步兵利險；

translations.literal: Wu young general Huan the General urged the king: "Wu has many infantry; infantry profit from rugged terrain;
translations.idiomatic: Wu young general Huan the General urged the king, "Wu has many foot soldiers; infantry do well in rugged terrain;

sentences.zh: 漢多車騎，車騎利平地，願大王所過城不下，直去，疾西據洛陽武庫，食敖倉粟，阻山河之險以令諸侯，雖無入關，天下固已定矣。

translations.literal: Han has many chariots and cavalry; chariots and cavalry profit from level ground. I wish that wherever the great king passes, if cities are not taken, pass straight through, hurry west to hold Luoyang's armory, eat Aocang's grain, block the peril of mountains and rivers to command the feudal lords—even without entering the passes, all under Heaven would already be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Han has many chariots and cavalry; chariots and cavalry do well on level ground. I urge that wherever Your Majesty passes, if a city is not taken, pass it by and press on—hurry west to seize Luoyang's armory, eat the grain of Aocang, and hold the mountain-and-river barriers to command the feudal lords; even without entering the passes, the realm would already be settled.

sentences.zh: 大王徐行留下城邑，漢軍車騎至，馳入梁、楚之郊，事敗矣。

translations.literal: If the great king moves slowly and leaves cities behind, when Han chariots and cavalry arrive and gallop into Liang and Chu's outskirts, the affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty moves slowly and leaves cities behind, when Han chariots and cavalry arrive and gallop into Liang and Chu's outskirts, all is lost.

sentences.zh: 」吳王問諸老將，老將曰：「此年少，椎鋒可耳，安知大慮！

translations.literal: " The King of Wu asked the various old generals; the old generals said: "This young fellow—good for smashing at the point, that's all; how would he know great deliberation!
translations.idiomatic: " The King of Wu asked the veteran generals; they said, "This young man is fit to smash the vanguard, nothing more—how would he know grand strategy!

sentences.zh: 」於是王不用桓將軍計。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the king did not use General Huan's plan.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the king did not adopt General Huan's plan.

sentences.zh: 王專並將兵。

translations.literal: The king personally combined command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: The king personally took sole command of the army.

sentences.zh: 兵未度淮，諸賓客皆得為將、校尉、候、司馬，獨周丘不用。

translations.literal: Before the army had crossed the Huai, all the guests could become generals, commandants, scouts, and marshals—only Zhou Qiu was not used.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army had crossed the Huai, every guest was made a general, commandant, scout, or marshal—only Zhou Qiu was passed over.

sentences.zh: 周丘者，下邳人，亡命吳，酤酒無行；

translations.literal: Zhou Qiu was a man of Xiapi; a fugitive in Wu, he sold wine and had no conduct;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qiu was a man of Xiapi, a fugitive in Wu who sold wine and lived without propriety;

sentences.zh: 王薄之，不任。

translations.literal: the king slighted him and did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: the king looked down on him and gave him no post.

sentences.zh: 周丘乃上謁，說王曰：「臣以無能，不得待罪行間。

translations.literal: Zhou Qiu thereupon went up to an audience and urged the king: "Your servant, lacking ability, could not wait on you among those guilty of crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qiu thereupon had an audience and urged the king, "Your servant, being without ability, could not serve you among those bearing criminal guilt.

sentences.zh: 臣非敢求有所將也，願請王一漢節，必有以報。

translations.literal: Your servant does not dare to ask to command troops; I wish to request one Han staff from the king—there will surely be repayment.
translations.idiomatic: I do not dare ask to command troops; I ask only for one Han staff from Your Majesty—I shall surely repay you.

sentences.zh: 」王乃予之。

translations.literal: " The king then gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: " The king then gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 周丘得節，夜馳入下邳；

translations.literal: Zhou Qiu obtained the staff; by night he galloped into Xiapi;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qiu obtained the staff and by night galloped into Xiapi;

sentences.zh: 下邳時聞吳反，皆城守。

translations.literal: Xiapi at the time had heard Wu rebelled and all fortified and defended.
translations.idiomatic: Xiapi had already heard that Wu had rebelled, and all were fortifying and defending.

sentences.zh: 至傳舍，召令入戶，使從者以罪斬令，遂召昆弟所善豪吏告曰：「吳反，兵且至，屠下邳不過食頃；

translations.literal: Reaching the relay station, he summoned the magistrate to enter; he had his followers execute the magistrate on a charge, then summoned his brothers and favored bold officers and told them: "Wu has rebelled, troops are about to arrive, slaughter of Xiapi would not exceed the time of a meal;
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the relay station, he summoned the magistrate inside and had his followers execute him on a charge; he then summoned his brothers and favored bold officers and said, "Wu has rebelled, troops are about to arrive, and Xiapi will be slaughtered within the time of a meal;

sentences.zh: 今先下，家室必完，能者封侯矣。

translations.literal: if you submit first, households will surely be preserved; the capable will be enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: submit first and your households will be spared; the capable will be enfeoffed as marquises.

sentences.zh: 」出，乃相告，下邳皆下。

translations.literal: " Going out, they told one another, and all Xiapi submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Going out, they spread the word, and all Xiapi submitted.

sentences.zh: 周丘一夜得三萬人，使人報吳王，遂將其兵北略城邑；

translations.literal: Zhou Qiu in one night obtained thirty thousand men, sent men to report to the King of Wu, and thereupon led his army north raiding cities;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qiu in one night raised thirty thousand men, sent word to the King of Wu, and thereupon led his troops north raiding cities;

sentences.zh: 比至陽城，兵十餘萬，破陽城中尉軍；

translations.literal: by the time he reached Yangcheng, troops exceeded one hundred thousand; he broke the Central Commandant's army at Yangcheng;
translations.idiomatic: by the time he reached Yangcheng his force exceeded one hundred thousand; he defeated the Central Commandant's army at Yangcheng;

sentences.zh: 聞吳王敗走，自度無與共成功，即引兵歸下邳，未至，疽發背死。

translations.literal: hearing the King of Wu was defeated and fleeing, he reckoned he had no one with whom to succeed together, thereupon led troops back to Xiapi; before arriving, an ulcer broke out on his back and he died.
translations.idiomatic: hearing the King of Wu was defeated and fleeing, he judged that he had no partner with whom to succeed, and led his troops back toward Xiapi; before he arrived, a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.

sentences.zh: ----6壬午晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: ----6 On renwu, the last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 On renwu, the last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: ----7吳王之棄軍亡也，軍遂潰，往往稍降太尉條侯及梁軍。

translations.literal: ----7 When the King of Wu abandoned his army and fled, the army thereupon collapsed; here and there they gradually submitted to Grand Commandant Marquis of Tiao and the army of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 When the King of Wu abandoned his army and fled, the army collapsed; here and there men gradually surrendered to Grand Commandant Marquis of Tiao and the army of Liang.

sentences.zh: 吳王渡淮，走丹徒，保東越，兵可萬餘人，收聚亡卒。

translations.literal: The King of Wu crossed the Huai, fled to Dantu, sheltered with Dongyue, troops about ten thousand and more, gathering scattered fugitive soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu crossed the Huai, fled to Dantu, and took refuge with Dongyue with a force of more than ten thousand, gathering scattered fugitives.

sentences.zh: 漢使人以利啖東越，東越即紿吳王出勞軍，使人鏦殺吳王，盛其頭，馳傳以聞。

translations.literal: Han sent men to bait Dongyue with profit; Dongyue then deceived the King of Wu to come out and comfort the army, sent men to spear-kill the King of Wu, packed his head, and galloped by relay to report.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent men to entice Dongyue with profit; Dongyue then tricked the King of Wu into coming out to review the troops, had him speared to death, packed his head, and galloped by relay to report.

sentences.zh: 吳太子駒亡走閩越。

translations.literal: The crown prince of Wu Ju fled to Minyue.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince of Wu, Ju, fled to Minyue.

sentences.zh: 吳、楚反，凡三月，皆破滅，於是諸將乃以太尉謀為是；

translations.literal: The Wu-Chu rebellion, altogether three months, all were broken and extinguished; thereupon the various generals then considered the Grand Commandant's plan correct;
translations.idiomatic: The Wu-Chu rebellion lasted three months in all before all were destroyed; thereupon the generals judged the Grand Commandant's plan correct;

sentences.zh: 然梁王由此與太尉有隙。

translations.literal: yet the King of Liang from this had a rift with the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: yet from this the King of Liang bore a grudge against the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 三王之圍臨菑也，齊王使路中大夫告於天子。

translations.literal: When the three kings besieged Linzi, the King of Qi sent an Imperial Messenger on the Road to report to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When the three kings besieged Linzi, the King of Qi sent an Imperial Messenger on the Road to report to the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天子復令路中大夫還報，告齊王堅守，「漢兵今破吳楚矣。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again ordered the Imperial Messenger on the Road to return and report, telling the King of Qi to hold firm: "Han troops have now broken Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven again ordered the Imperial Messenger on the Road to return with word telling the King of Qi to hold firm: "Han troops have now defeated Wu and Chu.

sentences.zh: 」路中大夫至，三國兵圍臨菑數重，無從入。

translations.literal: " When the Imperial Messenger on the Road arrived, the armies of the three states besieged Linzi in many rings; he could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Imperial Messenger on the Road arrived, the armies of the three states had Linzi encircled in many rings and he could not get in.

sentences.zh: 三國將與路中大夫盟曰：「若反言：『漢已破矣，齊趣下三國，不，且見屠。

translations.literal: The generals of the three states would ally with the Imperial Messenger on the Road, saying: "If you speak contrary: 'Han is already broken; Qi hurry and submit to the three states—if not, you will soon be slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: The generals of the three states made a pact with the Imperial Messenger on the Road, saying, "If you speak falsely: 'Han is already defeated; Qi must hurry and submit to the three states—if not, you will soon be slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 』」路中大夫既許，至城下，望見齊王曰：「漢已發兵百萬，使太尉亞夫擊破吳、楚，方引兵救齊，齊必堅守無下！

translations.literal: '" The Imperial Messenger on the Road having agreed, when he reached below the wall and saw the King of Qi, he said: "Han has already sent a million troops; the Grand Commandant Yafu has broken Wu and Chu and is just leading troops to rescue Qi—Qi must hold firm and not submit!
translations.idiomatic: '" The Imperial Messenger on the Road having agreed, when he reached the foot of the wall and saw the King of Qi, he said, "Han has already sent a million troops; Grand Commandant Yafu has defeated Wu and Chu and is leading troops to rescue Qi—Qi must hold firm and not submit!

sentences.zh: 」三國將誅路中大夫。

translations.literal: " The generals of the three states would execute the Imperial Messenger on the Road.
translations.idiomatic: " The generals of the three states would have executed the Imperial Messenger on the Road.

sentences.zh: 齊初圍急，陰與三國通謀，約未定；

translations.literal: At first when the siege was pressing, Qi secretly communicated conspiracy with the three states; the covenant was not settled;
translations.idiomatic: When the siege was first pressing, Qi secretly communicated with the three states; the agreement was not yet settled;

sentences.zh: 會路中大夫從漢來，其大臣乃復勸王無下三國。

translations.literal: when the Imperial Messenger on the Road came from Han, his great ministers thereupon again urged the king not to submit to the three states.
translations.idiomatic: when the Imperial Messenger on the Road came from Han, the great ministers again urged the king not to submit to the three states.

sentences.zh: 會漢將欒布、平陽侯等兵至齊，擊破三國兵。

translations.literal: When Han generals Luan Bu, Marquis of Pingyang, and others' troops reached Qi, they struck and broke the armies of the three states.
translations.idiomatic: When Han generals Luan Bu, Marquis of Pingyang, and others reached Qi with their troops, they defeated the armies of the three states.

sentences.zh: 解圍已，後聞齊初與三國有謀，將欲移兵伐齊。

translations.literal: After the siege was lifted, afterward they heard Qi at first had conspiracy with the three states; they were about to move troops to attack Qi.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege was lifted, they later heard that Qi had at first conspired with the three states and were about to move troops to attack Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊孝王懼，飲藥自殺。

translations.literal: King Xiao of Qi was afraid and drank poison and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiao of Qi, in fear, drank poison and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 膠西、膠東、菑川王各引兵歸國。

translations.literal: The kings of Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, and Zichuan each led troops back to their states.
translations.idiomatic: The kings of Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, and Zichuan each led their troops back to their states.

sentences.zh: 膠西王徒跣、席蒿、飲水謝太后。

translations.literal: The King of Jiaoxi went barefoot, spread artemisia as a mat, drank water, and apologized to the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Jiaoxi went barefoot, spread artemisia for a mat, drank water, and apologized to the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 王太子德曰：「漢兵還，臣觀之，已罷，可襲，願收王餘兵擊之！

translations.literal: The king's crown prince De said: "Han troops have returned; your servant observed them—they are already weary; they can be raided; I wish to gather the king's remaining troops and strike them!
translations.idiomatic: The king's crown prince De said, "Han troops have returned; I observed them—they are already exhausted and can be attacked; I ask to gather Your Majesty's remaining troops and strike them!

sentences.zh: 不勝而逃入海，未晚也。

translations.literal: If we do not win, fleeing into the sea is not yet late.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not win, fleeing to sea is not yet too late.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「吾士卒皆已壞，不可用。

translations.literal: " The king said: "My soldiers are all already ruined; they cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: " The king said, "My troops are all already ruined and cannot be used.

sentences.zh: 」弓高侯韓頹當遺膠西王書曰：「奉詔誅不義，降者赦除其罪，復故；

translations.literal: " Marquis of Gonggao Han Tuidang sent a letter to the King of Jiaoxi: "By edict we execute the unrighteous; those who submit are pardoned, their crimes removed, and restored to former status;
translations.idiomatic: " Marquis of Gonggao Han Tuidang sent a letter to the King of Jiaoxi: "By edict we punish the unrighteous; those who submit are pardoned, their crimes removed, and restored to former standing;

sentences.zh: 不降者滅之。

translations.literal: those who do not submit are extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: those who do not submit are destroyed.

sentences.zh: 王何處？

translations.literal: Where is the king?
translations.idiomatic: Where is the king?

sentences.zh: 須以從事。

translations.literal: We must deal with you accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: We must deal with you accordingly.

sentences.zh: 」王肉袒叩頭，詣漢軍壁謁曰：「臣卬奉法不謹，驚駭百姓，乃苦將軍遠道至於窮國，敢請菹醢之罪！

translations.literal: " The king went bare-chested and knocked his head, went to the Han army's rampart and called: "Your servant Ang failed to observe the law carefully, startled and terrified the hundred surnames, and thus troubled the general to come far on the road to this impoverished state—I dare request the crime of being minced into paste!
translations.idiomatic: " The king went bare-chested and knocked his head, went to the Han army's rampart and said, "Your servant Ang failed to observe the law carefully, startled and terrified the people, and thus troubled the general to come far to this impoverished state—I dare request the punishment of being minced into paste!

sentences.zh: 」弓高侯執金鼓見之曰：「王苦軍事，願聞王發兵狀。

translations.literal: " The Marquis of Gonggao held golden drums and received him, saying: "The king has suffered military matters; I wish to hear the state of the king's dispatching troops.
