translations.idiomatic: " The Marquis of Gonggao, holding golden drums, received him and said, "Your Majesty has suffered in war; I wish to hear how you raised your troops.

sentences.zh: 」王頓首膝行，對曰：「今者晁錯天子用事臣，變更高皇帝法令，侵奪諸侯地。

translations.literal: " The king knocked his head and crawled on his knees, replying: "Now Chao Cuo, the Son of Heaven's minister in power, changed and raised the August Emperor's laws and statutes, encroaching on and seizing feudal lords' lands.
translations.idiomatic: " The king knocked his head and crawled on his knees, replying, "Chao Cuo, the Son of Heaven's minister in power, has altered and raised the August Emperor's laws and statutes and encroached on and seized the feudal lords' lands.

sentences.zh: 卬等以為不義，恐其敗亂天下，七國發兵且誅錯。

translations.literal: Ang and others considered this unrighteous, feared he would corrupt and disorder all under Heaven; the seven states dispatched troops intending to execute Chao Cuo.
translations.idiomatic: Ang and others considered this unrighteous and feared he would throw the realm into disorder; the seven states raised troops to execute Chao Cuo.

sentences.zh: 今聞錯已誅，卬等謹已罷兵歸。

translations.literal: Now hearing Chao Cuo has been executed, Ang and others respectfully have already ceased troops and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Now that we hear Chao Cuo has been executed, Ang and others have respectfully already ceased our troops and returned.

sentences.zh: 」將軍曰：「王苟以錯為不善，何不以聞？

translations.literal: " The general said: "If the king truly considered Cuo not good, why not report it?
translations.idiomatic: " The general said, "If Your Majesty truly considered Cuo wrong, why did you not report it?

sentences.zh: 及未有詔、虎符，擅發兵擊義國？

translations.literal: And before there was an edict and tiger tally, presumptuously dispatch troops to strike righteous states?
translations.idiomatic: And before there was an edict and tiger tally, why did you presumptuously raise troops to attack loyal states?

sentences.zh: 以此觀之，意非徒欲誅錯也。

translations.literal: From this observing, the intent was not merely to execute Chao Cuo.
translations.idiomatic: Judging from this, your intent was not merely to execute Chao Cuo.

sentences.zh: 」乃出詔書，為王讀之，曰：「王其自圖！

translations.literal: " He thereupon produced the edict and read it for the king: "The king must consider for himself!
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon produced the edict and read it to the king: "Your Majesty must consider for yourself!

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「如卬等死有餘罪！

translations.literal: " The king said: "For Ang and others death leaves surplus guilt!
translations.idiomatic: " The king said, "For Ang and others death would still leave guilt to spare!

sentences.zh: 」遂自殺，太后、太子皆死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he killed himself; the empress dowager and crown prince both died.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he killed himself; the empress dowager and crown prince both died.

sentences.zh: 膠東王、菑川王、濟南王皆伏誅。

translations.literal: The kings of Jiaodong, Zichuan, and Jinan all were executed before the law.
translations.idiomatic: The kings of Jiaodong, Zichuan, and Jinan were all executed.

sentences.zh: 酈將軍兵至趙，趙王引兵還邯鄲城守。

translations.literal: General Li's troops reached Zhao; the King of Zhao led troops back to Handan and fortified the city to defend.
translations.idiomatic: General Li's troops reached Zhao; the King of Zhao led his troops back to Handan and held the city.

sentences.zh: 酈寄攻之，七月不能下。

translations.literal: Li Ji attacked it; seven months and he could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji besieged it for seven months without taking it.

sentences.zh: 匈奴聞吳、楚敗，亦不肯入邊。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu heard Wu and Chu were defeated and also would not enter the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu heard that Wu and Chu were defeated and also refused to cross the border.

sentences.zh: 欒布破齊還，並兵引水灌趙城。

translations.literal: Luan Bu, having broken Qi, returned, combined troops, and led water to flood the Zhao city.
translations.idiomatic: Luan Bu, having defeated Qi, returned, combined forces, and led water to flood the Zhao capital.

sentences.zh: 城壞，王遂自殺。

translations.literal: The city wall broke; the king thereupon killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: The walls collapsed; the king thereupon killed himself.

sentences.zh: 帝以齊首善，以迫劫有謀，非其罪也，召立齊孝王太子壽，是為懿王。

translations.literal: The emperor because Qi first did good, and its coercion and conspiracy had a plot not its own crime, summoned and established King Xiao of Qi's crown prince Shou—this was King Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because Qi had been the first to do right and its coercion and conspiracy were not its own doing, summoned and enthroned King Xiao of Qi's crown prince Shou as King Yi.

sentences.zh: 濟北王亦欲自殺，幸全其妻子。

translations.literal: The King of Jibei also wished to kill himself but fortunately preserved his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Jibei also wished to kill himself but was fortunate enough to preserve his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 齊人公孫玃謂濟北王曰：「臣請試為大王明說梁王，通意天子；

translations.literal: The Qi man Gongsun Yan said to the King of Jibei: "Your servant requests to try for the great king to clarify and speak to the King of Liang, conveying intent to the Son of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: The Qi man Gongsun Yan said to the King of Jibei, "Your servant asks to try to speak plainly for Your Majesty to the King of Liang and convey your intent to the Son of Heaven;

sentences.zh: 說而不用，死未晚也。

translations.literal: if persuasion is not used, death is not yet late.
translations.idiomatic: if he is not persuaded, death is not yet too late.

sentences.zh: 」公孫玃遂見梁王曰：「夫濟北之地，東接強齊，南牽吳、越，北脅燕、趙。

translations.literal: " Gongsun Yan thereupon saw the King of Liang: "The territory of Jibei—east it adjoins strong Qi, south it is dragged by Wu and Yue, north it is coerced by Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: " Gongsun Yan thereupon saw the King of Liang and said, "The territory of Jibei adjoins powerful Qi on the east, is pulled by Wu and Yue on the south, and is menaced by Yan and Zhao on the north.

sentences.zh: 此四分五裂之國。

translations.literal: This is a state split into four and five pieces.
translations.idiomatic: It is a land split four and five ways.

sentences.zh: 權不足以自守，勁不足以捍寇，又非有奇怪雲以待難也；

translations.literal: Its power is insufficient to defend itself, its strength insufficient to repel invaders, and moreover it lacks strange clouds to await calamity;
translations.idiomatic: Its authority is insufficient to defend itself, its strength insufficient to repel invaders, and it has no miraculous portents to await disaster;

sentences.zh: 雖墜言於吳，非其正計也。

translations.literal: though it fell in speech with Wu, that was not its proper plan.
translations.idiomatic: though it fell in with Wu in word, that was not its proper course.

sentences.zh: 鄉使濟北見情實，示不從之端，則吳必先歷齊，畢濟北，招燕、趙而總之，如此，則山東之從結而無隙矣。

translations.literal: Had Jibei shown true circumstances and displayed the start of not following, then Wu would first have passed through Qi, finished Jibei, summoned Yan and Zhao and gathered them—in such case the Shandong alliance would have been tied with no gap.
translations.idiomatic: Had Jibei shown its true circumstances and made clear that it would not follow, Wu would first have passed through Qi, finished Jibei, and summoned Yan and Zhao to gather them—then the Shandong alliance would have been knit without a gap.

sentences.zh: 今吳王連諸侯之兵，驅白徒之眾，西與天子急衡，濟北獨底節不下；

translations.literal: Now the King of Wu joined the feudal lords' troops, drove the masses of common levies, west urgently contended with the Son of Heaven, while Jibei alone held its integrity and would not submit;
translations.idiomatic: Now the King of Wu joined the feudal lords' armies, drove the masses of common levies, and pressed west to contend with the Son of Heaven, while Jibei alone held firm and would not submit;

sentences.zh: 使吳失與而無助，跬步獨進，瓦解土崩，破敗而不救者，未必非濟北之力也。

translations.literal: causing Wu to lose allies and have no aid, inch by inch advancing alone, collapsing like earth and disintegrating like a dam, broken and defeated with none to save—this was perhaps not without Jibei's force.
translations.idiomatic: causing Wu to lose allies and have no help, to advance alone step by step, and to collapse and break without rescue—this was perhaps not without Jibei's doing.

sentences.zh: 夫以區區之濟北而與諸侯爭強，是以羔犢之弱而扞虎狼之敵也。

translations.literal: For petty Jibei to contend for supremacy with the feudal lords is to use the weakness of lamb and calf to repel tiger and wolf enemies.
translations.idiomatic: For petty Jibei to contend for supremacy with the feudal lords is to pit the weakness of a lamb or calf against tiger-and-wolf foes.

sentences.zh: 守職不橈，可謂誠一矣。

translations.literal: Holding office without bending—this may be called sincere unity.
translations.idiomatic: Holding office without bending—this may be called single-minded loyalty.

sentences.zh: 功義如此，尚見疑於上，脅肩低首，累足撫衿，使有自悔不前之心，非社稷之利也。

translations.literal: Merit and righteousness such as this, yet still suspected above, shrugging shoulders and bowing head, piling feet and stroking the lapel, causing a mind of self-reproach and not advancing—this is not profit to the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: With merit and righteousness such as this, yet still suspected above, shrinking the shoulders and bowing the head, standing on tiptoe and clutching the lapel, until one has a mind to repent and not advance—this is not to the altars' benefit.

sentences.zh: 臣恐籓臣守職者疑之。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that feudatory officials holding office will doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant fears that feudatory lords who hold their posts faithfully will be put in doubt.

sentences.zh: 臣竊料之，能歷西山，徑長樂，抵未央，攘袂而正議者，獨大王耳。

translations.literal: Your servant privately reckons: able to pass Western Hills, go straight through Changle, reach Weiyang, roll up sleeves and speak uprightly—only the great king.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant privately judges that only Your Majesty can pass Western Hills, go straight through Changle, reach Weiyang Palace, roll up your sleeves, and speak forthrightly.

sentences.zh: 上有全亡之功，下有安百姓之名，德淪於骨髓，恩加於無窮，願大王留意詳惟之。

translations.literal: Above there is merit in wholly saving from death; below there is a name for settling the hundred surnames; virtue soaking into marrow and bones, grace extending without end—I wish the great king to pay attention and carefully consider.
translations.idiomatic: Above you would have the merit of wholly saving a man from death; below you would have the name of settling the people; virtue would soak to the marrow and grace extend without end—I urge Your Majesty to consider this carefully.

sentences.zh: 」孝王大悅，使人馳以聞；

translations.literal: " King Xiao was greatly pleased and sent men galloping to report;
translations.idiomatic: " King Xiao was greatly pleased and sent men galloping to report;

sentences.zh: 濟北王得不坐，徙封於菑川。

translations.literal: the King of Jibei was not punished by execution, and was moved and enfeoffed at Zichuan.
translations.idiomatic: the King of Jibei was not executed but was transferred and enfeoffed at Zichuan.

sentences.zh: ----8河間王太傅衛綰擊吳、楚有功，拜為中尉。

translations.literal: ----8 The Grand Tutor of the King of Hejian Wei Wan struck Wu and Chu with merit and was appointed Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 The Grand Tutor of the King of Hejian, Wei Wan, who had struck Wu and Chu with merit, was appointed Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 綰以中郎將事文帝，醇謹無它。

translations.literal: Wan as Central Palace General served Emperor Wen—pure, careful, and without other [faults].
translations.idiomatic: Wan served Emperor Wen as Central Palace General, pure and careful, with no other faults.

sentences.zh: 上為太子時，召文帝左右飲，而綰稱病不行。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was Crown Prince, he summoned Wen's close attendants to drink, but Wan claimed illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor was crown prince he summoned Wen's close attendants to drink, but Wan pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 文帝且崩，屬上曰：「綰長者，善遇之。

translations.literal: When Wen was about to die, he entrusted the Emperor, saying: "Wan is an elder—treat him well.
translations.idiomatic: As Wen lay dying he entrusted the Emperor, saying, "Wan is an elder—treat him well.

sentences.zh: 」故上亦寵任焉。

translations.literal: " Therefore the Emperor also favored and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Therefore the Emperor also favored and employed him.

sentences.zh: ----9夏，六月，乙亥，詔：「吏民為吳王濞等所詿誤當坐及逋逃亡軍者，皆赦之。

translations.literal: ----9 In summer, the sixth month, on yihai, an edict: "Officials and commoners misled by King of Wu Liu Pi and the rest who ought to be punished, and deserters who fled the army—all are pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 In summer, the sixth month, on the day yihai, an edict ran: "Officials and commoners misled by King of Wu Liu Pi and the rest who ought to be punished, and deserters who fled the army—all are pardoned.

sentences.zh: 」帝欲以吳王弟德哀侯廣之子續吳，以楚元王子禮續楚。

translations.literal: " The Emperor wished to continue Wu through the son of De'ai Marquis Guang, younger brother of the King of Wu, and to continue Chu through Prince Li of Chu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor wished to continue the Wu line through the son of De'ai Marquis Guang, the King of Wu's younger brother, and to continue Chu through Prince Li, son of King Yuan of Chu.

sentences.zh: 竇太后曰：「吳王，老人也，宜為宗室順善；

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Dou said: "The King of Wu is an old man who ought to have been compliant and good as a member of the imperial clan;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Dou said, "The King of Wu is an old man who ought to have been a compliant, dutiful kinsman of the house;

sentences.zh: 今乃首率七國紛亂天下，奈何續其後！

translations.literal: yet now he was first to lead the seven kingdoms in disordering all under Heaven—how can we continue his line!
translations.idiomatic: yet he was first to lead the seven kingdoms in throwing the realm into chaos—how can we continue his line!

sentences.zh: 」不許吳，許立楚後。

translations.literal: " She did not permit Wu; she permitted establishing a successor for Chu.
translations.idiomatic: " She refused Wu; she allowed a successor for Chu.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，徙淮陽王餘為魯王；

translations.literal: On yihai, Prince of Huaiyang Yu was moved to be King of Lu;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Prince Yu of Huaiyang was moved to be King of Lu;

sentences.zh: 南王非為江都王，王故吳地；

translations.literal: the King of the South Fei was made King of Jiangdu, ruling the former Wu territory;
translations.idiomatic: King Fei of the South was made King of Jiangdu, ruling the former Wu lands;

sentences.zh: 立宗正禮為楚王；

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan Li was installed as King of Chu;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Clan Li was installed as King of Chu;

sentences.zh: 立皇子端為膠西王，勝為中山王。

translations.literal: the Emperor's son Duan was installed as King of Jiaoxi and Sheng as King of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor's sons Duan and Sheng were installed as kings of Jiaoxi and Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: ----1春，復置關，用傳出入。

translations.literal: ----1 In spring, the passes were restored; travel permits were required for entry and exit.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In spring the passes were restored and travel permits were required for entry and exit.

sentences.zh: ----2夏，四月，己巳，立子榮為皇太子，徹為膠東王。

translations.literal: ----2 In summer, the fourth month, on jisi, the son Rong was installed as Crown Prince and Che as King of Jiaodong.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In summer, the fourth month, on the day jisi, the son Rong was installed as crown prince and Che as King of Jiaodong.

sentences.zh: ----3六月，赦天下。

translations.literal: ----3 In the sixth month, he pardoned all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the sixth month he proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: ----4秋，七月，臨江王閼薨。

translations.literal: ----4 In autumn, the seventh month, Prince of Linjiang Min died.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In autumn, the seventh month, Prince Min of Linjiang died.

sentences.zh: ----5冬，十月，戊戌晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: ----5 In winter, the tenth month, on the last day wuxu, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In winter, the tenth month, on the last day wuxu, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: ----6初，吳、楚七國反，吳使者至淮南，淮南王欲發兵應之。

translations.literal: ----6 At the beginning, when Wu and Chu and the seven kingdoms rebelled, Wu's envoy reached Huainan; the King of Huainan wished to mobilize troops to respond.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 At first, when Wu, Chu, and the seven kingdoms rebelled, Wu's envoy reached Huainan and the King of Huainan wished to raise troops in support.

sentences.zh: 其相曰：「王必欲應吳，臣願為將。

translations.literal: His chancellor said: "If Your Majesty must respond to Wu, your servant wishes to be general.
translations.idiomatic: His chancellor said, "If Your Majesty must answer Wu, your servant will serve as general.

sentences.zh: 」王乃屬之。

translations.literal: " The king thereupon entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: " The king thereupon entrusted him.

sentences.zh: 相已將兵，因城守，不聽王而為漢，漢亦使曲城侯將兵救淮南，以故得完。

translations.literal: Once the chancellor had taken command of the troops, he fortified and held the city, did not heed the king, and sided with Han; Han also sent Marquis of Qucheng with troops to rescue Huainan—therefore it was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Once the chancellor had the troops he walled the city and held it, ignored the king, and sided with Han; Han also sent Marquis of Qucheng with troops to relieve Huainan, and so it remained intact.

sentences.zh: 吳使者至廬江，廬江王不應，而往來使越。

translations.literal: When Wu's envoy reached Lujiang, the King of Lujiang did not respond but instead sent envoys back and forth to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu's envoy reached Lujiang the King of Lujiang did not respond but kept sending envoys to Yue.

sentences.zh: 至衡山，衡山王堅守無二心。

translations.literal: At Hengshan, the King of Hengshan held firm with no second intent.
translations.idiomatic: At Hengshan the King of Hengshan held firm and showed no divided loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及吳、楚已破，衡山王入朝。

translations.literal: When Wu and Chu had already been defeated, the King of Hengshan entered court.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu and Chu were defeated the King of Hengshan came to court.

sentences.zh: 上以為貞信，勞苦之，曰：「南方卑濕。

translations.literal: The Emperor took him to be steadfast and faithful, comforted him for his hardships, and said: "The south is low and damp.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged him steadfast and faithful, comforted him for his hardships, and said, "The south is low and damp.

sentences.zh: 」徙王王於濟北以褒之。

translations.literal: " He moved the king to be king at Jibei as a reward.
translations.idiomatic: " He moved him to be king of Jibei as a reward.

sentences.zh: 廬江王以邊越，數使使相交，徙為衡山王，王江北。

translations.literal: The King of Lujiang, because he bordered Yue and repeatedly sent envoys to exchange with them, was moved to be King of Hengshan, ruling north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Lujiang, because he bordered Yue and repeatedly exchanged envoys with them, was moved to be King of Hengshan, ruling north of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: ----1春，正月，作陽陵邑。

translations.literal: ----1 In spring, the first month, the Yangling settlement was built.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In spring, the first month, the Yangling settlement was built.

sentences.zh: 夏，募民徙陽陵，賜錢二十萬。

translations.literal: In summer, the people were recruited to move to Yangling; each was granted two hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: In summer commoners were recruited to move to Yangling, each granted two hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: ----2遣公主嫁匈奴單于。

translations.literal: ----2 A princess was sent to marry the Xiongnu chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 A princess was sent to marry the Xiongnu chanyu.

sentences.zh: ----3徙廣川王彭祖為趙王。

translations.literal: ----3 King Pengzu of Guangchuan was moved to be King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 King Pengzu of Guangchuan was moved to be King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: ----4濟北貞王勃薨。

translations.literal: ----4 Steadfast King Bo of Jibei died.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 Steadfast King Bo of Jibei died.

sentences.zh: ----1冬，十二月，雷，霖雨。

translations.literal: ----1 In winter, the twelfth month, there was thunder and soaking rain.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In winter, the twelfth month, there was thunder and soaking rain.

sentences.zh: ----2初，上為太子，薄太后以薄氏女為妃；

translations.literal: ----2 At the beginning, when the Emperor was crown prince, Empress Dowager Bo made a woman of the Bo clan his consort;
translations.idiomatic: ----2 At first, when the Emperor was crown prince, Empress Dowager Bo made a woman of the Bo clan his consort;

sentences.zh: 及即位，為皇后，無寵。

translations.literal: when he took the throne she became empress but had no favor.
translations.idiomatic: when he took the throne she became empress but won no favor.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，皇后薄氏廢。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, Empress Bo was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, Empress Bo was deposed.

sentences.zh: ----3楚文王禮薨。

translations.literal: ----3 King Wen Li of Chu died.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 King Wen Li of Chu died.

sentences.zh: ----4初，燕王臧荼有孫女曰臧兒，嫁為槐里王仲妻，生男信與兩女而仲死；

translations.literal: ----4 At the beginning, King Zang of Yan had a granddaughter named Zang Er, who married as wife to King Zhong of Huaili, bore a son Xin and two daughters, and then Zhong died;
translations.idiomatic: ----4 At first, King Zang of Yan had a granddaughter named Zang Er who married King Zhong of Huaili, bore a son Xin and two daughters, and then Zhong died;

sentences.zh: 更嫁長陵田氏，生男蚡、勝。

translations.literal: she remarried into the Tian clan of Changling and bore sons Fen and Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: she remarried into the Tian clan of Changling and bore sons Fen and Sheng.

sentences.zh: 文帝時，臧兒長女為金王孫婦，生女俗。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wen's time Zang Er's eldest daughter was wife to King Sun of Jin and bore a daughter Su.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wen's time Zang Er's eldest daughter was wife to King Sun of Jin and bore a daughter Su.

sentences.zh: 臧兒卜筮之，曰：「兩女皆當貴。

translations.literal: Zang Er divined by milfoil and said: "Both daughters are destined for eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Er divined by milfoil and was told, "Both daughters are destined for eminence.

sentences.zh: 」臧兒乃奪金氏婦，金氏怒，不肯予決；

translations.literal: " Zang Er then seized the wife from the Jin clan; the Jin clan was angry and would not grant a divorce;
translations.idiomatic: " Zang Er then seized her from the Jin household; the Jins were angry and would not grant a divorce;

sentences.zh: 內之太子宮，生男徹。

translations.literal: she brought her into the crown prince's palace, where she bore a son Che.
translations.idiomatic: she brought her into the crown prince's palace, where she bore a son Che.

sentences.zh: 徹方在身時，王夫人夢日入其懷。

translations.literal: While Che was still in the womb, Lady Wang dreamed the sun entered her bosom.
translations.idiomatic: While Che was still in the womb, Lady Wang dreamed the sun entered her bosom.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，長男榮為太子。

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the throne, the eldest son Rong was crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor took the throne, the eldest son Rong was crown prince.

sentences.zh: 其母栗姬，齊人也。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Li was a woman of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Li was from Qi.

sentences.zh: 長公主嫖欲以女嫁太子，栗姬以後宮諸美人皆因長公主見帝，故怒而不許；

translations.literal: The Eldest Princess Piao wished to marry her daughter to the crown prince; Lady Li, because the various beauties of the inner palace all reached the Emperor through the Eldest Princess, was angry and would not agree;
translations.idiomatic: The Eldest Princess Piao wished to marry her daughter to the crown prince; Lady Li, because the palace beauties all reached the Emperor through the Eldest Princess, was angry and refused;

sentences.zh: 長公主欲與王夫人男徹，王夫人許之。

translations.literal: the Eldest Princess wished to give her daughter to Lady Wang's son Che, and Lady Wang agreed.
translations.idiomatic: the Eldest Princess then sought Lady Wang's son Che, and Lady Wang agreed.

sentences.zh: 由是長公主日讒栗姬而譽王夫人男之美；

translations.literal: therefore the Eldest Princess daily slandered Lady Li while praising the beauty of Lady Wang's son;
translations.idiomatic: thereafter the Eldest Princess daily slandered Lady Li while praising Lady Wang's son;

sentences.zh: 帝亦自賢之，又有曩者所夢日符，計未有所定。

translations.literal: the Emperor also himself considered him worthy, and again there was the former dream-sign of the sun—his deliberation had not yet been settled.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor also considered him worthy himself, and again there was the earlier dream-sign of the sun—yet he had not decided.

sentences.zh: 王夫人知帝嗛栗姬，因怒未解，陰使人趣大行請立栗姬為皇后。

translations.literal: Lady Wang knew the Emperor resented Lady Li and that his anger was not yet resolved; she secretly had someone urge the Grand Master of Ceremonies to request installing Lady Li as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang knew the Emperor resented Lady Li and that his anger had not cooled; she secretly had someone urge the Grand Master of Ceremonies to request that Lady Li be made empress.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「是而所宜言邪！

translations.literal: The Emperor angrily said: "Is this what you ought to speak!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor angrily said, "Is this what you ought to say!

sentences.zh: 」遂按誅大行。

translations.literal: " He thereupon investigated and executed the Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon investigated and executed the Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: ----1冬，十一月，己酉，廢太子榮為臨江王。

translations.literal: ----1 In winter, the eleventh month, on jiyou, the crown prince Rong was deposed and made King of Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In winter, the eleventh month, on the day jiyou, Crown Prince Rong was deposed and made King of Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 太子太傅竇嬰力爭不能得，乃謝病免。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Tutor Dou Ying strove in argument but could not prevail and thereupon pleaded illness and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Tutor Dou Ying argued fiercely but could not prevail and thereupon pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 栗姬恚恨而死。

translations.literal: Lady Li died of resentment and hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li died of resentment and grief.

sentences.zh: ----2庚寅晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: ----2 On the last day gengyin, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 On the last day gengyin, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: ----3二月，丞相陶青免。

translations.literal: ----3 In the second month, Chancellor Tao Qing was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the second month Chancellor Tao Qing was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，太尉周亞夫為丞相。

translations.literal: On yisi, Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu became Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu became chancellor.

sentences.zh: 罷太尉官。

translations.literal: The office of Grand Commandant was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The office of grand commandant was abolished.

sentences.zh: ----4夏，四月，乙巳，立皇后王氏。

translations.literal: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, on yisi, Lady Wang was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, on yisi, Lady Wang was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: ----5丁巳，立膠東王徹為皇太子。

translations.literal: ----5 On dingsi, King Che of Jiaodong was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 On dingsi King Che of Jiaodong was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: ----6是歲，以太僕劉舍為御史大夫，濟南太守郅都為中尉。

translations.literal: ----6 This year, Grand Master of the Palace Liu She was made Grandee Secretary and Administrator of Jinan Zhi Du was made Commandant of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 That year Grand Master of the Palace Liu She was made grandee secretary and Administrator of Jinan Zhi Du was made commandant of the capital.

sentences.zh: 始，都為中郎將，敢直諫。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Du was Central Palace General, he dared to remonstrate bluntly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Du was Central Palace General, he dared to remonstrate bluntly.

sentences.zh: 嘗從入上林，賈姬如廁，野彘卒來入廁。

translations.literal: Once when he followed the Emperor into the Shanglin Park, Lady Jia went to the privy and a wild boar suddenly came in.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he followed the Emperor into the Shanglin Park, Lady Jia went to the privy and a wild boar suddenly burst in.

sentences.zh: 上目都，都不行；

translations.literal: the Emperor signaled Du with his eyes, but neither moved;
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor signaled Du with his eyes, but neither moved;

sentences.zh: 上欲自持兵救賈姬。

translations.literal: the Emperor wished to take up arms himself to rescue Lady Jia.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor wished to seize a weapon himself to rescue Lady Jia.

sentences.zh: 都伏上前曰：「亡一姬，復一姬進，天下所少，寧賈姬等乎！

translations.literal: Du prostrated himself forward and said: "Lose one lady and another enters—the realm lacks little; would Your Majesty value Lady Jia and the like!
translations.idiomatic: Du prostrated himself before the Emperor and said, "Lose one lady and another takes her place—the realm lacks little; would Your Majesty risk yourself for Lady Jia!

sentences.zh: 陛下縱自輕，奈宗廟、太后何！

translations.literal: Your Majesty may lightly esteem yourself, but what of the ancestral temple and the Empress Dowager!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty may hold your own life cheap, but what of the ancestral temple and the empress dowager!

sentences.zh: 」上乃還，彘亦去。

translations.literal: " The Emperor thereupon returned, and the boar also left.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor thereupon withdrew, and the boar also left.

sentences.zh: 太后聞之，賜都金百斤，由此重都。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager heard it she granted Du a hundred jin of gold; from this he was highly valued.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager heard of it she granted Du a hundred jin of gold; from then on he was highly valued.

sentences.zh: 都為人，勇悍公廉，不發私書，問遺無所受，請謁無所聽。

translations.literal: Du as a man was fierce, incorrupt, and public-minded; he sent no private letters, accepted no gifts in inquiry, and heard no private petitions.
translations.idiomatic: Du was fierce, upright, and incorrupt; he sent no private letters, accepted no gifts, and heard no private petitions.

sentences.zh: 及為中尉，先嚴酷，行法不避貴戚。

translations.literal: When he became Commandant of the Capital, he was first severe and harsh, enforcing law without avoiding noble kin.
translations.idiomatic: As commandant of the capital he was first severe and harsh, enforcing the law without sparing noble kin.

sentences.zh: 列侯、宗室見都，側目而視，號曰「蒼鷹」。

translations.literal: Ranked marquises and members of the imperial clan, seeing Du, looked sideways at him and called him "Dark Hawk."
translations.idiomatic: Ranked marquises and imperial clansmen looked askance at him and called him "Dark Hawk."

sentences.zh: ----1夏，四月，乙巳，赦天下。

translations.literal: ----1 In summer, the fourth month, on yisi, he pardoned all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In summer, the fourth month, on yisi, he proclaimed a general amnesty.

translations.literal: ----2 There was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 There was an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 衡山原都雨雹，大者尺八寸。

translations.literal: At Yuandu in Hengshan hail fell as large as one foot eight inches.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuandu in Hengshan hail fell as large as one foot eight inches across.

sentences.zh: ----1春，二月，匈奴入燕。

translations.literal: ----1 In spring, the second month, the Xiongnu entered Yan.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In spring, the second month, the Xiongnu raided Yan.

sentences.zh: ----2三月，臨江王榮坐侵太宗廟壖垣為宮，征詣中尉府對簿。

translations.literal: ----2 In the third month, Prince Rong of Linjiang was charged with encroaching on the high founder's temple embankment to build a palace; he was summoned to the Commandant's office for trial.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In the third month Prince Rong of Linjiang was charged with encroaching on the high founder's temple embankment to build a palace and was summoned to the commandant's office for trial.

sentences.zh: 臨江王欲得刀筆，為書謝上，而中尉郅都禁吏不予；

translations.literal: The Prince of Linjiang wished to obtain brush and knife to write a letter apologizing to the Emperor, but Commandant Zhi Du forbade the clerks to give them;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rong of Linjiang wished to obtain brush and knife to write a letter of apology to the Emperor, but Commandant Zhi Du forbade the clerks to supply them;

sentences.zh: 魏其侯使人間與臨江王。

translations.literal: Marquis of Weiji sent a man secretly to communicate with the Prince of Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Weiji sent a man secretly to communicate with Prince Rong of Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 臨江王既為書謝上，因自殺。

translations.literal: Once the Prince of Linjiang had written the letter apologizing to the Emperor, he thereupon killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Once Prince Rong had written his letter of apology to the Emperor, he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 竇太后聞之，怒，後竟以危法中都而殺之。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Dou heard it she was angry; later she finally had Du killed by applying a dangerous law against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Dou heard of it she was furious; later she had Du killed by applying a dangerous law against him.

sentences.zh: ----3夏，四月，有星孛於西北。

translations.literal: ----3 In summer, the fourth month, a broom star appeared in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In summer, the fourth month, a comet appeared in the northwest.

sentences.zh: ----4立皇子越為廣川王，寄為膠東王。

translations.literal: ----4 The Emperor's sons Yue and Ji were installed as kings of Guangchuan and Jiaodong.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 The Emperor's sons Yue and Ji were installed as kings of Guangchuan and Jiaodong.

sentences.zh: ----5秋，九月，甲戌晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: ----5 In autumn, the ninth month, on the last day jiaxu, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In autumn, the ninth month, on the last day jiaxu, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: ----6初，梁孝王以至親有功，得賜天子旌旗。

translations.literal: ----6 At the beginning, King Xiao of Liang, because he was a close kinsman with merit, was granted the Son of Heaven's banners and flags.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 At first King Xiao of Liang, as a close kinsman with merit, was granted the Son of Heaven's banners and flags.

sentences.zh: 從千乘萬騎，出蹕入警。

translations.literal: He went forth with a thousand chariots and ten thousand horsemen; when he exited the road was cleared and when he entered guards were posted.
translations.idiomatic: He went forth with a thousand chariots and ten thousand horsemen; when he went out the road was cleared and when he entered guards were posted.

sentences.zh: 王寵信羊勝、公孫詭，以詭為中尉。

translations.literal: The king favored and trusted Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui, making Gui his commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The king favored Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui and made Gui his commandant.

sentences.zh: 勝、詭多奇邪計，欲使王求為漢嗣。

translations.literal: Sheng and Gui had many strange and crooked schemes and wished to make the king seek to become heir to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and Gui devised many strange, crooked schemes and wished to make the king seek to become heir to Han.

sentences.zh: 栗太子之廢也，太后意欲以梁王為嗣，嘗因置酒謂帝曰：「安車大駕，用梁王為寄。

translations.literal: When the Li crown prince was deposed, the Empress Dowager wished to make the King of Liang the heir; once at a feast she told the Emperor: "The cushioned carriage and great escort—entrust them to the King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Li was deposed the empress dowager wished to make the King of Liang the heir; once at a feast she told the Emperor, "The cushioned carriage and great escort—entrust them to the King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 」帝跪席舉身曰：「諾。

translations.literal: " The Emperor knelt on the mat and raised his body, saying: "Yes.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor knelt on the mat and straightened up, saying, "Yes.

sentences.zh: 」罷酒，帝以訪諸大臣，大臣袁盎等曰：「不可。

translations.literal: " When the wine was ended the Emperor consulted the great ministers; Minister Yuan Ang and others said: "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: " When the feast ended the Emperor consulted the great ministers; Minister Yuan Ang and others said, "It cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 昔宋宣公不立子而立弟，以生禍亂，五世不絕。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Xuan of Song did not install his son but installed his younger brother, thereby producing calamity and disorder that did not cease for five generations.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Duke Xuan of Song did not install his son but installed his younger brother, thereby producing calamity and disorder that did not cease for five generations.

sentences.zh: 小不忍，害大義，故《春秋》大居正。

translations.literal: Small impatience harms great principle—therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals greatly honors dwelling in the correct succession.
translations.idiomatic: Small impatience harms great principle—therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals greatly honors the rightful succession.

sentences.zh: 」由是太后議格，遂不復言。

translations.literal: " From this the Empress Dowager's deliberation was blocked, and she did not speak of it again.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the empress dowager's plan was blocked, and she spoke of it no more.

sentences.zh: 王又嘗上書；

translations.literal: The king also once submitted a memorial;
translations.idiomatic: The king also once submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 「願賜容車之地，徑至長樂宮，自梁國士眾築作甬道朝太后。

translations.literal: "I beg grant of land for a covered carriage route straight to Changle Palace, and that troops and people of Liang build a covered corridor-way to attend the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: "I beg land for a covered carriage route straight to Changle Palace, and that Liang's troops and people build a covered corridor to attend the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 」袁盎等皆建以為不可。

translations.literal: " Yuan Ang and the rest all advised that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Ang and the rest all advised that it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 梁王由此怨袁盎及議臣，乃與羊勝、公孫詭謀，陰使人刺殺袁盎及他議臣十餘人。

translations.literal: The King of Liang thereby resented Yuan Ang and the deliberating ministers; he then plotted with Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui, secretly sending men to assassinate Yuan Ang and more than ten other deliberating ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Liang thereby resented Yuan Ang and the ministers who had opposed him; he plotted with Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui and secretly sent men to assassinate Yuan Ang and more than ten other opposing ministers.

sentences.zh: 賊未得也，於是天子意梁；

translations.literal: The assassins had not yet been captured; the Son of Heaven thereupon suspected Liang;
translations.idiomatic: The assassins had not yet been caught, and the Son of Heaven thereupon suspected Liang;

sentences.zh: 逐賊，果梁所為。

translations.literal: when they pursued the assassins, it turned out to have been done by Liang.
translations.idiomatic: when the assassins were pursued, it proved to have been Liang's doing.

sentences.zh: 上遣田叔、呂委主往按梁事，捕公孫詭、羊勝；

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Tian Shu and Lü Weizhu to go investigate the Liang affair and arrest Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng;
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor sent Tian Shu and Lü Weizhu to investigate the Liang affair and arrest Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng;

sentences.zh: 詭、勝匿王后宮，使者十餘輩至梁，責二千石急。

translations.literal: Gui and Sheng hid in the queen's inner palace; more than ten envoy parties reached Liang, urgently pressing the two-thousand-dan officials.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and Sheng hid in the queen's inner palace; more than ten envoy parties reached Liang and urgently pressed the two-thousand-dan officials.

sentences.zh: 梁相軒丘豹及內史韓安國以下舉國大索，月餘弗得。

translations.literal: Liang Chancellor Xuanqiu Bao, Interior Minister Han Anguo, and those below mounted a nationwide search for more than a month without finding them.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chancellor Xuanqiu Bao, Interior Minister Han Anguo, and the rest mounted a nationwide search for more than a month without finding them.

sentences.zh: 安國聞詭、勝匿王所，乃入見王而泣曰：「主辱者臣死。

translations.literal: Anguo heard that Gui and Sheng were hiding at the king's place; he then entered to see the king and weeping said: "When the lord is shamed, ministers die.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo heard that Gui and Sheng were hiding with the king; he entered to see the king and weeping said, "When the lord is shamed, ministers die.

sentences.zh: 大王無良臣，故紛紛至此。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has no good ministers—hence things have come to such disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has no good ministers, and so things have come to such disorder.

sentences.zh: 今勝、詭不得，請辭，賜死！

translations.literal: Now that Sheng and Gui cannot be found, I request to resign—grant me death!
translations.idiomatic: Now that Sheng and Gui cannot be found, I beg to resign—grant me death!

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「何至此！

translations.literal: " The king said: "How reach such a point!
translations.idiomatic: " The king said, "How could it come to this!

sentences.zh: 」安國泣數行下，曰：「大王自度於皇帝，孰與臨江王親？

translations.literal: " Anguo weeping several lines of tears, said: "Your Majesty, judge yourself against the Emperor—who is closer, you or the King of Linjiang?
translations.idiomatic: " Anguo wept freely and said, "Your Majesty, judge yourself against the Emperor—which of you is closer to him, you or the King of Linjiang?

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「弗如也。

translations.literal: " The king said: "I am not as close.
translations.idiomatic: " The king said, "I am not as close.

sentences.zh: 」安國曰：「臨江王鱣長太子，以一言過，廢王臨江；

translations.literal: " Anguo said: "The King of Linjiang was the grown crown prince; for a single fault of speech he was deposed and made king of Linjiang;
translations.idiomatic: " Anguo said, "The King of Linjiang was the grown crown prince; for a single fault of speech he was deposed and made king of Linjiang;

sentences.zh: 用宮垣事，卒自殺中尉府。

translations.literal: over the palace rampart affair he finally killed himself at the Commandant's office.
translations.idiomatic: over the palace rampart affair he finally killed himself at the commandant's office.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 治天下終不用私亂公。

translations.literal: Governing all under Heaven ultimately does not use private ties to disorder public law.
translations.idiomatic: Governing the realm ultimately does not let private ties disorder public law.

sentences.zh: 今大王列在諸侯，訹邪臣浮說，犯上禁，橈明法。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty ranks among the feudal lords; vicious evil ministers make floating speeches, violating superior prohibitions and bending clear law.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty ranks among the feudal lords; vicious ministers spread reckless talk, violate imperial prohibitions, and bend clear law.

sentences.zh: 天子以太后故，不忍致法於大王；

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven because of the Empress Dowager cannot bear to apply the law to Your Majesty;
translations.idiomatic: the Son of Heaven, because of the empress dowager, cannot bear to apply the law to Your Majesty;

sentences.zh: 太后日夜涕泣，幸大王自改，大王終不覺寤。

translations.literal: the Empress Dowager day and night weeps tears, hoping Your Majesty will reform yourself—Your Majesty ultimately does not awaken.
translations.idiomatic: the empress dowager weeps day and night, hoping Your Majesty will reform yourself—yet Your Majesty never awakens to it.

sentences.zh: 有如太后宮車即晏駕，大王尚誰攀乎？

translations.literal: Should the Empress Dowager's palace carriage soon reach evening departure, whom would Your Majesty still cling to?
translations.idiomatic: Should the empress dowager's palace carriage soon depart on its final journey, whom would Your Majesty still have to cling to?

sentences.zh: 」語未卒，王泣數行而下，謝安國曰：「吾今出勝、詭。

translations.literal: " Before the words were finished the king wept several lines of tears and said in apology to Anguo: "I will now hand over Sheng and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: " Before he finished speaking the king wept freely and apologized to Anguo, "I will now hand over Sheng and Gui.

sentences.zh: 」王乃令勝、詭皆自殺，出之。

translations.literal: " The king then ordered Sheng and Gui both to kill themselves and handed them over.
translations.idiomatic: " The king then ordered Sheng and Gui both to kill themselves and handed their bodies over.

sentences.zh: 上由此怨望梁王。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereby bore resentment toward the King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereby bore resentment toward the King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 梁王恐，使鄒陽入長安，見皇后兄王信說曰：「長君弟得幸於上，後宮莫及；

translations.literal: The King of Liang was afraid; he sent Zou Yang into Chang'an to see the Empress's elder brother Wang Xin and persuade him, saying: "Chief Excellency, your younger sister is favored by the Emperor—none in the inner palace can match her;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Liang was afraid; he sent Zou Yang into Chang'an to see the empress's elder brother Wang Xin and said, "Chief Excellency, your younger sister is favored by the Emperor—none in the inner palace can match her;

sentences.zh: 而長君行跡多不循道理者。

translations.literal: yet Chief Excellency, your conduct often does not follow reason.
translations.idiomatic: yet Chief Excellency, your conduct often does not follow reason.

sentences.zh: 今袁盎事即究竟，梁王伏誅，太后無所發怒，切齒側目於貴臣，竊為足下憂之。

translations.literal: Now that the Yuan Ang affair is about to be concluded, the King of Liang will submit to execution; the Empress Dowager will have nowhere to vent her anger—she will gnash teeth and look askance at noble ministers; I privately worry for you.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Yuan Ang affair is about to be concluded, the King of Liang will submit to execution; the empress dowager will have nowhere to vent her anger and will gnash her teeth and look askance at noble ministers—I privately worry for you.

sentences.zh: 」長君曰：「為之奈何？

translations.literal: " Chief Excellency said: "What is to be done about it?
translations.idiomatic: " Chief Excellency said, "What is to be done about it?

sentences.zh: 」陽曰：「長君誠能精為上言之，得毋竟梁事；

translations.literal: " Yang said: "If Chief Excellency can truly speak to the Emperor with care, the Liang affair may not be concluded;
translations.idiomatic: " Yang said, "If Chief Excellency can truly speak carefully to the Emperor, the Liang affair may not be concluded;

sentences.zh: 長君必固自結於太后，太后厚德長君入於骨髓，而長君之弟幸於兩宮，金城之固也。

translations.literal: Chief Excellency will surely firmly bind himself to the Empress Dowager; the Empress Dowager's deep virtue toward Chief Excellency will enter to the marrow, and Chief Excellency's younger sister is favored in both palaces—a solidity like a metal city wall.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Excellency will surely bind himself firmly to the empress dowager; her deep favor toward you will enter to the marrow, and your younger sister is favored in both palaces—a solidity like walls of bronze.

sentences.zh: 昔者舜之弟象，日以殺舜為事，及舜立為天子，封之於有卑。

translations.literal: Formerly Shun's younger brother Xiang daily made killing Shun his business; when Shun was installed as Son of Heaven he enfeoffed him at Youbei.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Shun's younger brother Xiang daily made killing Shun his business; when Shun was installed as Son of Heaven he enfeoffed him at Youbei.

sentences.zh: 夫仁人之于兄弟，無藏怒，無宿怨，厚親愛而已。

translations.literal: For benevolent men toward brothers: no hidden anger, no stored resentment—only thick kin-love.
translations.idiomatic: For benevolent men toward brothers there is no hidden anger and no stored resentment—only deep kin-love.

sentences.zh: 是以後世稱之。

translations.literal: Therefore later ages praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore later ages praise him.

sentences.zh: 以是說天子，徼幸梁事不奏。

translations.literal: Use this to persuade the Son of Heaven, hoping perchance the Liang affair will not be reported.
translations.idiomatic: Use this to persuade the Son of Heaven, hoping perchance the Liang affair will not be reported.

sentences.zh: 」長君曰：「諾。

translations.literal: " Chief Excellency said: "Agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Chief Excellency said, "Agreed.

sentences.zh: 」乘間入言之。

translations.literal: " Seizing an interval he entered and spoke it.
translations.idiomatic: " Seizing an opportunity he entered and spoke to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝怒稍解。

translations.literal: The Emperor's anger gradually eased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's anger gradually eased.

sentences.zh: 是時，太后憂梁事不食，日夜泣不止，帝亦患之。

translations.literal: At this time the Empress Dowager, distressed over the Liang affair, would not eat and wept day and night without cease; the Emperor also was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the empress dowager, distressed over the Liang affair, would not eat and wept day and night without cease; the Emperor was troubled as well.

sentences.zh: 會田叔等按梁事來還，至霸昌廄，取火悉燒梁之獄辭，空手來見帝。

translations.literal: When Tian Shu and the rest investigating the Liang affair came back, at Bachang Stable they took fire and burned all of Liang's prison records entirely, and came empty-handed to see the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Shu and the rest investigating the Liang affair returned, at Bachang Stable they took fire and burned all of Liang's case records, then came empty-handed to see the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「梁有之乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Did Liang have involvement?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Did Liang have involvement?

sentences.zh: 」叔對曰：「死罪。

translations.literal: " Shu replied: "A capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: " Shu replied, "A capital offense.

sentences.zh: 有之。

translations.literal: There was.
translations.idiomatic: There was.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「其事安在？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Where is the matter?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "Where is the evidence?

sentences.zh: 」田叔曰：「上毋以梁事為問也。

translations.literal: " Tian Shu said: "Your Majesty, do not ask about the Liang affair.
translations.idiomatic: " Tian Shu said, "Your Majesty, do not ask about the Liang affair.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「何也？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Why?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "Why?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「今梁王不伏誅，是漢法不行也；

translations.literal: " He said: "Now if the King of Liang does not submit to execution, Han law is not enforced;
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "Now if the King of Liang does not submit to execution, Han law is not enforced;

sentences.zh: 伏法而太后食不甘味，臥不安席，此憂在陛下也。

translations.literal: if he submits to the law the Empress Dowager will find food not sweet and sleep not restful on her mat—this worry rests on Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: if he submits to the law the empress dowager will find no pleasure in food and no rest on her mat—this worry rests on Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」上大然之，使叔等謁太后，且曰：「梁王不知也。

translations.literal: " The Emperor greatly approved; he had Shu and the rest call on the Empress Dowager, saying moreover: "The King of Liang did not know.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor greatly approved; he had Shu and the rest call on the empress dowager, saying moreover, "The King of Liang did not know.

sentences.zh: 造為之者，獨在幸臣羊勝、公孫詭之屬為之耳，謹已伏誅死，梁王無恙也。

translations.literal: What was made was solely done by the favored ministers Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, and their sort; they have respectfully submitted to execution and died—the King of Liang is unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: What was done was solely the work of the favored ministers Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, and their sort; they have respectfully been executed and died—the King of Liang is unharmed.

sentences.zh: 」太后聞之，立起坐餐，氣平復。

translations.literal: " When the Empress Dowager heard it she immediately rose and sat to eat; her breath calmed and she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: " When the empress dowager heard it she immediately rose and sat down to eat; her breath calmed and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 梁王因上書請朝。

translations.literal: The King of Liang thereupon submitted a memorial requesting court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Liang thereupon submitted a memorial requesting an audience at court.

sentences.zh: 既至關，茅蘭說王，使乘布車，從兩騎入，匿於長公主園。

translations.literal: When he reached the pass, Mao Lan persuaded the king to ride a cloth-covered carriage with two riders following, enter, and hide in the Eldest Princess's garden.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the pass, Mao Lan persuaded the king to ride a plain cloth carriage with only two riders, enter, and hide in the Eldest Princess's garden.

sentences.zh: 漢使使迎王，王已入關，車騎盡居外，不知王處。

translations.literal: Han sent envoys to welcome the king; the king had already entered the pass—chariots and horsemen all remained outside, not knowing where the king was.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent envoys to welcome the king; the king had already entered the pass while his chariots and horsemen all remained outside, not knowing where he was.

sentences.zh: 太后泣曰：「帝果殺吾子！

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wept: "The Emperor has truly killed my son!
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager wept, "The Emperor has truly killed my son!

sentences.zh: 」帝憂恐。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was anxious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was anxious and afraid.

sentences.zh: 於是梁王伏斧質於闕下謝罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon the King of Liang prostrated himself with axe and block beneath the palace gate to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the King of Liang prostrated himself with axe and block beneath the palace gate to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 太后、帝大喜，相泣，復如故，悉召王從官入關。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager and Emperor were greatly pleased, wept toward each other, were restored as before, and summoned all the king's attendants to enter the pass.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager and Emperor were greatly pleased, wept toward each other, were restored as before, and summoned all the king's attendants to enter the pass.

sentences.zh: 然帝益疏王，不與同車輦矣。

translations.literal: Yet the Emperor increasingly kept the king at a distance and did not ride in the same carriage with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Emperor increasingly kept the king at a distance and no longer rode in the same carriage with him.

sentences.zh: 帝以田叔為賢，擢為魯相。

translations.literal: The Emperor took Tian Shu to be worthy and promoted him to Chancellor of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged Tian Shu worthy and promoted him to chancellor of Lu.

sentences.zh: ----1冬，十一月，罷諸侯御史大夫官。

translations.literal: ----1 In winter, the eleventh month, the office of Grandee Secretary among the feudal lords was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In winter, the eleventh month, the office of grandee secretary among the feudal lords was abolished.

translations.literal: ----2 In summer, the fourth month, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In summer, the fourth month, there was an earthquake.

translations.literal: ----3 In drought, the sale of wine was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In drought, the sale of wine was forbidden.

sentences.zh: ----4三月，丁巳，立皇子乘為清河王。

translations.literal: ----4 In the third month, on dingsi, the Emperor's son Cheng was installed as King of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In the third month, on dingsi, the Emperor's son Cheng was installed as King of Qinghe.

translations.literal: ----5 In autumn, the ninth month, there were locusts.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In autumn, the ninth month, locusts appeared.

sentences.zh: ----6有星孛於西北。

translations.literal: ----6 A broom star appeared in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 A comet appeared in the northwest.

sentences.zh: ----7戊戌晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: ----7 On the last day wuxu, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 On the last day wuxu, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: ----8初，上廢栗太子，周亞夫固爭之，不得；

translations.literal: ----8 At the beginning, when the Emperor deposed the Li crown prince, Zhou Yafu strove in argument but could not prevail;
translations.idiomatic: ----8 At first, when the Emperor deposed Crown Prince Li, Zhou Yafu argued fiercely but could not prevail;

sentences.zh: 上由此疏之。

translations.literal: the Emperor thereby kept him at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor thereby kept him at a distance.

sentences.zh: 而梁孝王每朝，常與太后言條侯之短。

translations.literal: Yet King Xiao of Liang, whenever he attended court, often spoke to the Empress Dowager of Marquis of Tiao's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever King Xiao of Liang attended court he often told the empress dowager of Marquis of Tiao's faults.

sentences.zh: 竇太后曰：「皇后兄王信可侯也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Dou said: "The Empress's elder brother Wang Xin may be ennobled.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Dou said, "The empress's elder brother Wang Xin may be ennobled.

sentences.zh: 」帝讓曰：「始，南皮、章武，先帝不侯，及臣即位乃侯之；

translations.literal: " The Emperor remonstrated: "At first Nanpi and Zhangwu—the late Emperor did not ennoble them; only when your servant took the throne were they ennobled;
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor objected, "At first Nanpi and Zhangwu—the late Emperor did not ennoble them; only when I took the throne were they ennobled;

sentences.zh: 信未得封也。

translations.literal: Xin has not yet received a fief.
translations.idiomatic: Xin has not yet received a fief.

sentences.zh: 」竇太后曰：「人生各以時行耳。

translations.literal: " Empress Dowager Dou said: "In life each acts according to his time.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Dowager Dou said, "In life each acts according to his time.

sentences.zh: 自竇長君在時，竟不得侯，死後，其子彭祖顧得侯，吾甚恨之！

translations.literal: When Chief Dou was alive he ultimately could not be ennobled; after death his son Pengzu alone was ennobled—I deeply resent it!
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Dou was alive he ultimately could not be ennobled; after his death only his son Pengzu was ennobled—I deeply resent it!

sentences.zh: 帝趣侯信也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, hasten to ennoble Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, hasten to ennoble Xin.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「請得與丞相議之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "I beg leave to deliberate with the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "Let me deliberate with the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 上與丞相議。

translations.literal: The Emperor deliberated with the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor deliberated with the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 亞夫曰：「高皇帝約：『非劉氏不得王，非有功不得侯。

translations.literal: Yafu said: "The High Emperor's covenant: 'None but the Liu clan may be king; none without merit may be ennobled.
translations.idiomatic: Yafu said, "The High Emperor's covenant: 'None but the Liu clan may be king; none without merit may be ennobled.

sentences.zh: 』今信雖皇后兄，無功，侯之，非約也。

translations.literal: ' Now though Xin is the Empress's elder brother, without merit—to ennoble him is not the covenant.
translations.idiomatic: ' Now though Xin is the empress's elder brother, without merit—to ennoble him violates the covenant.

sentences.zh: 」帝默然而止。

translations.literal: " The Emperor fell silent and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor fell silent and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 其後匈奴王徐廬等六人降，帝欲侯之以勸後。

translations.literal: Afterward the Xiongnu kings Xu Lu and five others surrendered; the Emperor wished to ennoble them to encourage those who followed.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Xiongnu kings Xu Lu and five others surrendered; the Emperor wished to ennoble them to encourage future defectors.

sentences.zh: 丞相亞夫曰：「彼背主降陛下，陛下侯之，則何以責人臣不守節者乎？

translations.literal: Chancellor Yafu said: "They betrayed their lord and surrendered to Your Majesty—if Your Majesty ennobles them, how will you reproach subjects who do not hold to their integrity?
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yafu said, "They betrayed their lord and surrendered to Your Majesty—if Your Majesty ennobles them, how will you reproach subjects who fail to hold to their integrity?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「丞相議不可用。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "The Chancellor's deliberation cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "The chancellor's advice cannot be followed.

sentences.zh: 」乃悉封徐廬等為列侯。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ennobled Xu Lu and the rest all as ranked marquises.

sentences.zh: 見廣，以為誘騎，皆驚，上山陳。

translations.idiomatic: Seeing Guang they took him for a decoy force; all were alarmed and went up a hill to form ranks.

sentences.zh: 廣之百騎皆大恐，欲馳還走。

translations.idiomatic: Guang's hundred horsemen were terrified and wished to gallop back and flee.

sentences.zh: 廣曰：「吾去大軍數十里，今如此以百騎走，匈奴追射我立盡。

sentences.zh: 今我留，匈奴必以我為大軍之誘，必不敢擊我。

translations.idiomatic: If we stay the Xiongnu will surely take us for the main army's decoy and will not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 」廣令諸騎曰：「前！

translations.literal: " Guang ordered the horsemen: "Forward!
translations.idiomatic: " Guang ordered the horsemen, "Forward!

sentences.zh: 」未到匈奴陣二里所，止，令曰：「皆下馬解鞍！

translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Li Guang rejoined his main army.
