translations.idiomatic: " The officials pressed him ever more harshly.

sentences.zh: 初，吏捕亞夫，亞夫欲自殺，其夫人止之，以故不得死，遂入廷尉，因不食五日，歐血而死。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when the officials seized Yafu, Yafu wished to kill himself; his wife stopped him, and for this reason he did not die; he then entered the Court Commandant's office and, for not eating five days, vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the officials first seized Yafu he wished to kill himself; his wife stopped him, so he did not die then; he entered the Court Commandant's custody and, after five days without food, vomited blood and died.

sentences.zh: ----9是歲，濟陰哀王不識薨。

translations.literal: ----9 This year, Lamented King Bushi of Jiyin died.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 That year Lamented King Bushi of Jiyin died.

sentences.zh: ----1春，正月，地一日三動。

translations.literal: ----1 In spring, the first month, the earth shook three times in one day.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In spring, the first month, the earth shook three times in one day.

sentences.zh: ----2三月，匈奴入雁門，太守馮敬與戰，死。

translations.literal: ----2 In the third month, the Xiongnu entered Yanmen; Administrator Feng Jing fought them and died.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In the third month the Xiongnu entered Yanmen; Administrator Feng Jing fought them and died.

sentences.zh: 發車騎、材官屯雁門。

translations.literal: Chariots, cavalry, and materiel troops were dispatched to garrison Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Chariotry, cavalry, and materiel troops were dispatched to garrison Yanmen.

sentences.zh: ----3春，以歲不登，禁內郡食馬粟；

translations.literal: ----3 In spring, because the year did not yield a good harvest, the inner commanderies were forbidden to feed horses on grain;
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In spring, because the harvest failed, the inner commanderies were forbidden to feed horses on grain;

sentences.zh: 沒入之。

translations.literal: what was used was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: any grain so used was confiscated.

sentences.zh: ----4夏，四月，詔曰：「雕文刻鏤，傷農事者也；

translations.literal: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, an edict said: "Carved patterns and cut inlay injure agricultural work;
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, an edict ran: "Carved ornament and fine chasing injure farming;

sentences.zh: 錦繡纂組，害女工者也。

translations.literal: brocade, embroidery, and gathered weave harm women's work.
translations.idiomatic: brocade, embroidery, and fine weaving harm women's work.

sentences.zh: 農事傷則饑之本，女工害則寒之原也。

translations.literal: When agricultural work is injured, that is the root of famine; when women's work is harmed, that is the source of cold.
translations.idiomatic: When farming is injured that is the root of famine; when women's work is harmed that is the source of cold.

sentences.zh: 夫饑寒並至而能亡為非者寡矣。

translations.literal: When hunger and cold come together, those who can perish without doing wrong are few.
translations.idiomatic: When hunger and cold come together, few can avoid wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 朕親耕，後親桑，以奉宗廟粢盛、祭服，為天下先；

translations.literal: We personally plow; the empress personally tends mulberry, to supply the ancestral temple grain offerings and sacrificial robes, taking the lead for all under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: We personally plow and the empress personally tends the mulberry, to supply the ancestral temple offerings and sacrificial robes, setting the example for the realm;

sentences.zh: 不受獻，減太官，省繇賦，欲天下務農蠶，素有蓄積，以備災害。

translations.literal: we do not accept tribute offerings, reduce the Grand Provisioner, and lighten corvée and taxes, wishing all under Heaven to devote themselves to farming and sericulture, always to have stores, and to prepare against disasters.
translations.idiomatic: we accept no tribute offerings, reduce the grand provisioner, and lighten corvée and taxes, wishing the realm to devote itself to farming and sericulture, always to keep stores, and to prepare against disaster.

sentences.zh: 強毋攘弱，眾毋暴寡；

translations.literal: the strong must not seize from the weak; the many must not tyrannize the few;
translations.idiomatic: the strong must not seize from the weak; the many must not bully the few;

sentences.zh: 老耆以壽終，幼孤得遂長。

translations.literal: the aged complete their years; the young and orphaned are enabled to grow up.
translations.idiomatic: the aged may end their years in peace; the young and orphaned may grow up.

sentences.zh: 今歲或不登，民食頗寡，其咎安在？

translations.literal: This year the harvest may not succeed; the people's food is rather scant—where does the fault lie?
translations.idiomatic: This year the harvest may fail and the people's food is scant—where does the fault lie?

sentences.zh: 或詐偽為吏，以貨賂為市，漁奪百姓，侵牟萬民。

translations.literal: Some falsely pose as officials, make bribery their market, fish and seize from the hundred surnames, and encroach upon and extort the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: Some pose falsely as officials, trade in bribery, plunder the people, and prey upon the masses.

sentences.zh: 縣丞，長吏也；

translations.literal: The county assistant is a chief official;
translations.idiomatic: The county assistant is a chief official;

sentences.zh: 奸法與盜盜，甚無謂也！

translations.literal: to twist the law and join with thieves in theft is very meaningless!
translations.idiomatic: to twist the law and join thieves in stealing is utterly senseless!

sentences.zh: 其令二千石各修其職；

translations.literal: Let the two-thousand-bushel officials each repair their duties;
translations.idiomatic: Let every two-thousand-bushel official attend to his duty;

sentences.zh: 不事官職、耗亂者，丞相以聞，請其罪。

translations.literal: those who do not attend to office duties and waste and disorder—let the Chancellor report and request their punishment.
translations.idiomatic: whoever neglects his office and causes waste and disorder—the chancellor is to report him and request punishment.

sentences.zh: 佈告天下，使明知朕意。

translations.literal: Proclaim this to all under Heaven so that all clearly know Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim this throughout the realm so that all may clearly know Our intent.

sentences.zh: 」----5五月，詔貲算四得官。

translations.literal: " ----5 In the fifth month, an edict: those whose property-tax assessment reached the fourth grade might obtain office.
translations.idiomatic: " ----5 In the fifth month an edict ran: those whose property-tax assessment reached the fourth grade might obtain office.

translations.literal: ----6 In autumn, great drought.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In autumn there was great drought.

sentences.zh: ----1冬，十月，日月皆食，赤五日。

translations.literal: ----1 In winter, the tenth month, both sun and moon were eclipsed; [the sky] was red five days.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In winter, the tenth month, both sun and moon were eclipsed and the sky stayed red five days.

sentences.zh: ----2十二月晦，雷；

translations.literal: ----2 On the last day of the twelfth month, thunder;
translations.idiomatic: ----2 On the last day of the twelfth month there was thunder;

sentences.zh: 日如紫；

translations.literal: the sun was like purple;
translations.idiomatic: the sun looked purple;

sentences.zh: 五星逆行守大微；

translations.literal: the five planets moved retrograde and guarded Great Supreme Palace;
translations.idiomatic: the five planets moved retrograde and guarded the Great Supreme Palace;

sentences.zh: 月貫天廷中。

translations.literal: the moon pierced through the Celestial Court.
translations.idiomatic: the moon pierced through the Celestial Court.

sentences.zh: ----3春，正月，詔曰：「農，天下之本也。

translations.literal: ----3 In spring, the first month, an edict said: "Agriculture is the root of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In spring, the first month, an edict ran: "Agriculture is the root of all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 黃金、珠、玉，饑不可食，寒不可衣，以為幣用，不識其終始。

translations.literal: Gold, pearls, and jade—when hungry they cannot be eaten, when cold they cannot be worn; used as currency, one does not know their beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, pearls, and jade cannot be eaten when hungry or worn when cold; used as currency, one cannot tell where they begin or end.

sentences.zh: 間歲或不登，意為末者眾，農民寡也。

translations.literal: In some years the harvest fails; we suspect many pursue secondary trades and farmers are few.
translations.idiomatic: In some years the harvest fails; we suspect too many pursue secondary trades and too few remain farmers.

sentences.zh: 其令郡國務勸農桑，益種樹，可得衣食物。

translations.literal: Let commanderies and kingdoms earnestly encourage farming and sericulture, increase planting of trees, and obtain clothing and food.
translations.idiomatic: Let commanderies and kingdoms earnestly encourage farming and sericulture, plant more trees, and secure clothing and food.

sentences.zh: 吏發民若取庸采黃金、珠、玉者，坐贓為盜。

translations.literal: Officials who mobilize the people yet take payment to gather gold, pearls, and jade are convicted of embezzlement as thieves.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who mobilize the people yet take fees to gather gold, pearls, and jade shall be convicted of embezzlement as thieves.

sentences.zh: 二千石聽者，與同罪。

translations.literal: Grand administrators who heed it share the same crime.
translations.idiomatic: Grand administrators who allow it share the same crime.

sentences.zh: 」----4甲寅，皇太子冠。

translations.literal: " ----4 On jiayin, the crown prince received the capping.
translations.idiomatic: " ----4 On jiayin the crown prince received the capping.

sentences.zh: ----5甲子，帝崩於未央宮。

translations.literal: ----5 On jiazi, the Emperor died in Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 On jiazi the Emperor died in Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 太子即皇帝位，年十六。

translations.literal: The crown prince assumed the imperial throne; he was sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince took the throne; he was sixteen.

sentences.zh: 尊皇太后為太皇太后，皇后為皇太后。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager and the empress as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager and the empress as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: ----6二月，癸酉，葬孝景皇帝於陽陵。

translations.literal: ----6 In the second month, on guiyou, Emperor Xiaojing was buried at Yangling.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In the second month, on guiyou, Emperor Xiaojing was buried at Yangling.

sentences.zh: 三月，封皇太后同母弟田蚡為武安侯，勝為周陽侯。

translations.literal: In the third month, the empress dowager's younger brother by the same mother Tian Fen was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wu'an and Sheng as Marquis of Zhouyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the empress dowager's uterine younger brothers Tian Fen and Sheng were enfeoffed as marquises of Wu'an and Zhouyang.

sentences.zh: ::班固贊曰：孔子稱：「斯民也，三代之所以直道而行也。

translations.literal: :: Ban Gu's praise says: Confucius said: "It is this people for whom the Three Dynasties walked the straight Way.
translations.idiomatic: :: Ban Gu's praise says: Confucius said, "It is this people for whom the Three Dynasties walked the straight Way.

sentences.zh: 」信哉！

translations.literal: " How true!
translations.idiomatic: " How true!

sentences.zh: 周、秦之敝，罔密文峻，而奸軌不勝，漢興，掃除煩苛，與民休息；

translations.literal: The failings of Zhou and Qin were nets dense and statutes severe, yet wicked paths could not be overcome; when Han arose it swept away vexatious harshness and rested the people;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Qin failed through dense nets and severe statutes, yet wicked ways could not be overcome; when Han arose it swept away vexatious harshness and let the people rest;

sentences.zh: 至於孝文，加這以恭儉；

translations.literal: As for Emperor Wen, upon this he added reverence and thrift;
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen reverence and thrift were added upon this;

sentences.zh: 孝景遵業。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing followed his enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing followed his course.

sentences.zh: 五六十載之間，至於移風易俗，黎民醇厚。

translations.literal: Within fifty or sixty years, customs were transformed and the common people grew pure and thick.
translations.idiomatic: Within fifty or sixty years customs were transformed and the common people grew pure and steadfast.

sentences.zh: 周雲成、康，漢言文、景，美矣！

translations.literal: Zhou spoke of Cheng and Kang; Han spoke of Wen and Jing—how beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Zhou spoke of Cheng and Kang; Han spoke of Wen and Jing—how fine!

sentences.zh: ::漢興，接秦之弊，作業劇而財匱，自天子不能具鈞駟，而將相或乘牛車，齊民無藏蓋。

translations.literal: :: When Han arose it took over Qin's failings; labor was intense and wealth depleted—even the Son of Heaven could not assemble a matched team of four, while generals and chancellors sometimes rode ox-carts, and the common people had nothing stored.
translations.idiomatic: :: When Han arose it inherited Qin's ruin; labor was intense and wealth depleted—even the Son of Heaven could not assemble a matched four-horse team, while generals and chancellors sometimes rode ox-carts and commoners had nothing stored.

sentences.zh: 天下已平，高祖乃令賈人不得衣絲、乘車，重租稅以困辱之。

translations.literal: When all under Heaven was settled, Gaozu then ordered merchants not to wear silk or ride carriages, and imposed heavy rents and taxes to distress and humiliate them.
translations.idiomatic: Once the realm was settled, Gaozu ordered merchants not to wear silk or ride carriages and imposed heavy rents and taxes to distress and humiliate them.

sentences.zh: 孝惠、高後時，為天下初定，復馳商賈之律；

translations.literal: In the times of Emperor Hui and Empress Gao, because the realm was newly settled, the laws restraining merchants were relaxed again;
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui and Empress Gao, because the realm was newly settled, the laws restraining merchants were relaxed again;

sentences.zh: 然市井之子孫，亦不得仕宦為吏。

translations.literal: yet descendants of market folk still could not enter office and serve as officials.
translations.idiomatic: yet descendants of market folk still could not enter office as officials.

sentences.zh: 量吏祿，度官用，以賦於民。

translations.literal: Official salaries were measured and government expenses estimated, then levied upon the people.
translations.idiomatic: Official salaries were measured and government expenses estimated, then levied upon the people.

sentences.zh: 而山川、園池、市井租稅之入，自天子以至於封君湯沐邑，皆各為私奉養焉，不領於天下之經費。

translations.literal: Yet revenue from mountains and rivers, parks and ponds, and market rents—from the Son of Heaven down to enfeoffed lords' bath towns—each served private maintenance and did not enter the realm's regular expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet revenue from mountains, rivers, parks, ponds, and market rents—from the Son of Heaven down to enfeoffed lords' bath towns—each served private maintenance and did not enter the realm's regular budget.

sentences.zh: 漕轉山東粟以給中都官，歲不過數十萬石。

translations.literal: Grain from east of the mountains was transported by water to supply the capital officials; each year it did not exceed several hundred thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Grain from east of the mountains was shipped to supply the capital officials; each year it did not exceed several hundred thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 繼以孝文、孝景，清淨恭儉，安養天下，七十餘年之間，國家無事，非遇水旱之災，民則人給家足。

translations.literal: Succeeding them, Emperors Wen and Jing were pure, reverent, and thrifty, peacefully nurturing all under Heaven; for more than seventy years the state had no troubles, and unless water or drought struck, the people had enough for each person and each household.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Wen and Jing, pure, reverent, and thrifty, the realm was peacefully nurtured; for more than seventy years the state had no troubles, and unless flood or drought struck, each person and household had enough.

sentences.zh: 都鄙廩庾皆滿，而府庫餘貨財；

translations.literal: Granaries in capital and countryside were all full, and the treasuries had surplus goods and wealth;
translations.idiomatic: Granaries in capital and countryside were full, and the treasuries held surplus goods and wealth;

sentences.zh: 京師之錢累巨萬，貫朽而不可校；

translations.literal: cash in the capital piled in tens of thousands; strings rotted and could not be counted;
translations.idiomatic: cash in the capital piled in the tens of thousands; strings rotted and could not be counted;

sentences.zh: 太倉之粟陳陳相因，充溢露積於外，至腐敗不可食。

translations.literal: grain in the Grand Granary lay layer upon layer, overflowing and piled in the open until it rotted and could not be eaten.
translations.idiomatic: grain in the Grand Granary lay layer upon layer, overflowing and piled in the open until it rotted and could not be eaten.

sentences.zh: 眾庶街巷有馬，而阡陌之間成群，乘字牝者擯而不得聚會。

translations.literal: Among the multitude, lanes and alleys had horses, and between field paths they gathered in herds; those riding mares with foals at foot were barred and could not join gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: Among the common people lanes and alleys had horses and field paths teemed with herds; riders of mares with foals at foot were barred from gatherings.

sentences.zh: 守閭閻者食粱肉，為吏者長子孫，居官者以為姓號。

translations.literal: Gatekeepers of neighborhood wards ate fine grain and meat; those serving as officials raised sons and grandsons; those in office took it as surname and title.
translations.idiomatic: Neighborhood gatekeepers ate fine grain and meat; officials raised sons and grandsons; office became family name and title.

sentences.zh: 故人人自愛而重犯法，先行義而後絀辱焉。

translations.literal: Therefore each person cherished himself and held the law in weight, putting righteousness first and punishment and disgrace after.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore each person cherished himself and held the law dear, putting righteousness first and punishment and disgrace after.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，罔疏而民富，役財驕溢，或至兼併；

translations.literal: At this time nets were loose and the people rich; wielding wealth with arrogant excess, some even reached merger and absorption;
translations.idiomatic: At this time laws were loose and the people rich; wielding wealth with arrogant excess, some even absorbed their neighbors;

sentences.zh: 豪黨之徒，以武斷於鄉曲。

translations.literal: men of powerful factions adjudicated by force in villages and hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: powerful factions adjudicated by force in villages and hamlets.

sentences.zh: 宗室有土，公、卿、大夫以下，爭於奢侈，室廬、輿服僭於上，無限度。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen held fiefs; from dukes, ministers, and grand masters downward they strove in luxury—dwellings, carriages, and dress exceeding their superiors without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen held fiefs; from dukes, ministers, and grand masters downward they strove in luxury—dwellings, carriages, and dress exceeding their superiors without limit.

sentences.zh: 物盛而衰，固其變也。

translations.literal: When things flourish they decline—such change is fixed.
translations.idiomatic: When things flourish they decline—such change is fixed.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，孝武內窮侈靡，外攘夷狄，天下蕭然，財力耗矣！

translations.literal: From this onward, Emperor Wu internally exhausted himself in extravagance and externally campaigned against the Yi and Di; all under Heaven grew desolate and financial strength was spent!
translations.idiomatic: From then on Emperor Wu internally exhausted the realm in extravagance and externally campaigned against the barbarians; the realm grew desolate and its wealth was spent!
